Which Mac desktop should you buy?

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Mac mini M6: Best desktop for most people
The new M6 Mac mini is our default desktop recommendation. It starts at $899/£899 and is ideal for home offices, general productivity, coding, photo editing and less demanding creative work. Because it launched only in September, a significant Prime Day discount would be particularly attractive.
Mac mini M5 Pro: Best compact professional desktop
Choose the M5 Pro model if you need more CPU and GPU performance, Thunderbolt 5, greater memory bandwidth or more than 32GB of unified memory.
Mac Studio M5 Max: Best professional workstation
The M5 Max Mac Studio offers considerably greater GPU performance, more memory and more connectivity than the Mac mini and is our preferred Studio configuration for most professional users.
iMac: Best all-in-one
The M4 iMac remains the obvious choice if you want an integrated 4.5K display and minimal desk clutter, but its older M4 chip and $1,499/£1,499 starting price mean we’d only recommend it with a substantial discount.
For more advice read:
Should I buy a Mac mini?
Should I buy a Mac Studio?


						

							


Prime Day Mac & MacBook deals to avoid
The cheapest Mac isn’t always the best value. Rather than using Prime Day simply to spend less, use it as an opportunity to get better specifications for the same budget.
When buying a Mac in 2026, try to get as much RAM and storage as you can afford. Most current Macs now start with 16GB of unified memory, although some still have only 256GB of storage. The main exception for memory is the entry-level MacBook Neo, which has 8GB of RAM and a 256GB SSD.
Because Apple silicon Macs can’t have their unified memory or internal storage upgraded later, it’s worth buying enough for your future needs. Memory is particularly important for demanding creative work, development and AI workloads.
For most buyers, prioritizing memory will provide greater long-term benefits than paying extra for a faster processor. Professional users may want 36GB or more, while 64GB or more can be worthwhile for demanding video production, software development and AI workloads.
Don’t buy a MacBook Neo simply because it’s the cheapest Mac: If an M5 Air is only around $200/£200 more, the Air gives you 16GB RAM, better display support and considerably more headroom.
Don’t pay close to full price for an M4 Mac mini: It has now been replaced. Clearance is only attractive if the discount properly reflects that.
Don’t confuse M6 Mac mini with M5 Pro Mac mini: M6 is the mainstream chip; M5 Pro remains much faster for many professional workloads despite the apparently older number. Macworld
Don’t buy a MacBook Pro purely because the discount looks enormous: Apple increased MSRP dramatically in June, so a “$400 off” deal may simply bring it closer to what the machine cost before the increase. Compare the actual selling price with the historic lows in your table.


						

							


Should you buy a MacBook or Mac during Prime Day?
October Prime Day is a good opportunity to buy a Mac, but whether you should take a deal depends on the model.
The M5 MacBook Air is particularly easy to recommend because it is not expected to be replaced until 2027. The new M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini are also safe purchases from a product-cycle perspective, although their recent launch means discounts may initially be smaller.
MacBook Pro buyers have a more difficult decision. The current M5 models are powerful machines and a large discount may outweigh the benefit of waiting, but a redesigned MacBook Pro is rumored before the end of 2026.
MacBook Neo buyers should watch the price closely. The previous Prime Day low was $589.99/£549, so a deal near or below those figures would be especially attractive.
We would avoid the iMac because of it’s typically high price and age. 
Finally, remember that Amazon isn’t the only retailer likely to cut prices during Prime Day. Best Buy, Walmart and B&H in the U.S., and retailers including Currys, John Lewis and others in the U.K., may run competing promotions, so compare prices before buying.
Before you buy, keep the following in mind:
Prime membership is required: Many of the best deals are exclusive to Amazon Prime members. If you’re not already subscribed, you might be able to take advantage of Amazon’s 30-day free trial or you could sign up for a month and cancel afterward. As well as getting free two-day shipping, Prime customers also get access to Prime Video and Music. Prime memberships cost $139 / £95 annually, or $14.99 / £8.99 / AU$6.99 every month. 
Other sales: If you miss Prime Day, you’ll have another chance to save during the Black Friday sales in November.
Student Discounts: Students can get discounts at Apple’s Education Store. See: Apple’s U.S. Education Store or Apple’s U.K. Education Store.
Prime Day is available in multiple countries, including Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, China, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Luxembourg, Mexico, the Netherlands, Portugal, Singapore, Spain, the U.K., and the U.S.



						

							


Why you can trust Macworld’s recommendations
The MacBooks and Mac desktops picked here are all chosen by our editors, who have decades of experience with Apple devices. We’ve reviewed everything we recommend, and we only highlight deals that are genuinely good value.
The products selected in this article are at the best current price, usually at or near all-time low prices, and we’ve selected what we think is the best configuration for each product type. We know Apple is expensive, so we’ve chosen products at prices we would be willing to pay, so you can trust that our recommendations will steer you in the right direction.

title: iOS 27.2 beta 3 is out now with the new Health app and more
content:
Macworld





Just a couple days after the wide release of iOS 27, Apple has released the first beta of iOS 27.2. That’s not a typo: it’s iOS 27.2, not 27.1. We never saw a 27.1 release, but Apple is beginning beta tests for the 27.2 branch.
This likely has something to do with the iPhone Duo, which is going on sale in October. We know the iPhone Duo will come with iOS 27.1, but we don’t yet know if any other devices will ever get a 27.1 update, or when all the devices will get on the same version together.
Update October 5: The third beta release is out now, shoring up bugs on the way to a wide release later this month.
What’s new in iOS 27.2
As beta testers report new capabilities in this version, we’ll report them here. 
New Health app: The 27.2 beta includes the new Health app, with a totally new redesign and AI-powered health insights.
Siri AI languages: Apple said that Siri AI, which launched supporting only U.S. English, will expand to French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish in October.
Dual Capture for Group FaceTime: Users can stream their front and rear cameras at the same time during FaceTime calls.
Podcasts Up Next: Up Next has been refreshed with two rows at the top of the Home tab: New Episodes and Continue Playing.
Simple Profiles on iOS/iPadOS/web: The Apple TV feature that lets you use multiple different account profiles now works in the Apple TV app on iOS, iPadOS, and the web.
Multiview in Apple TV: The feature that lets you watch four select sports streams at the same time on Apple TV now works on the Apple TV app on iOS.
iOS 27.2: How to install the public beta
If you want to test the iOS 27 beta releases but are not a registered developer, follow these steps:
Click Sign Up on the Apple Beta page and register with your Apple ID.
Log in to the Beta Software Program.
Click Enroll your iOS device.
Open the Settings app, tap General, then Software Update.
In the Beta Updates section, select the iOS Public Beta.
It may take a few moments after registering for the beta option to appear in Software Update.
iOS 27.2: How to install the developer beta
You’ll need to be registered as an Apple developer, but a free developer account will do. You can get one via Xcode or the Apple Developer app in iOS. Here’s how to do it via the Apple Developer app:
Download the Apple Developer App from the App Store.
Open the app.
Tap on Account.
Sign in using your usual Apple ID.

title: Apple Cash Adds ID Check for Reloads, Teases Bank Funding
content:
Apple Cash will soon require identity verification to add money. In emails going out to customers, Apple explains that starting on November 9, Green Dot Bank will begin requiring users to verify their identity when reloading their Apple Cash cards.


Identity verification is already required when adding, sending, or receiving over $500 total, but verification for any reload is new. Apple says Green Dot Bank may make it easier to add money to an Apple Cash card by introducing support for transferring funds from a bank or merchant in the future.

Right now, reloading an Apple Cash card can only be done through the Wallet app using a connected debit or prepaid card.

iOS 27 and who live in a state with support for digital driver's licenses can use a license stored in the Wallet app for identity verification.

Customers whose identity can't be verified will not be able to send or receive money or add money to an Apple Cash balance. Money already in an Apple Cash account can still be used for transactions or transferred to a bank account.

Apple says identity verification is required for "fraud protection and regulatory reasons."

title: Check out New Balance’s secret tribute to Steve Jobs on the anniversary of his passing
content:
Macworld





On this day 15 years ago, the world lost Steve Jobs after a years-long battle with pancreatic cancer. You’ll read many posts throughout the day about what a great leader and visionary he was, but none will be sweeter or more poignant than the subtle tribute New Balance posted.
If you ever watched one of Steve Jobs’ keynotes, you know his trademark outfit: a black turtleneck, blue jeans, black socks, and a pair of gray New Balance 992s. It’s not flashy or bold, but came to define his brand as much as the products he helped create.
New Balance hasn’t changed the look of the 992 since that time, and it’s still offered in the same “Grey with white” colorway. If you head over there to buy one, you’ll see a photo at the end of the gallery of a person sitting cross-legged wearing a pair. They happen to be wearing blue jeans with black socks and sitting in a black leather chair.

				
					

				
			
Steve Jobs shown wearing the New Balance 992 in Gray (right) next to New Balance’s re-creation of the pose.

Foundry




If you know your Apple history, you’ll recognize that this is the same chair that Steve Jobs famously sat in to conduct the first demo of the original iPad in January 2010. He wanted to show how casual and “intimate” the device was, so he used as if one would while in their home. It would be one of the last times we saw him on stage and one of his most iconic keynotes.
On this day, the image is an especially poignant and a touching tribute to a man who made the shoe famous.

title: The upcoming touchscreen MacBook Pro may be Air-light
content:
Macworld





After years of rumors and speculation, it looks like the first MacBook Pro with a touchscreen is finally almost here. If the latest leaks are to be believed, the device is currently in testing within Apple on macOS 27.2, and should arrive within the next month or so.
This new MacBook Pro won’t just be a current model with a touchscreen. We are expecting a full redesign of Apple’s iconic laptop: visually distinct, with an OLED display, Dynamic Island cutout, and of course a touchscreen. There are design and functionality changes to macOS to support touch, too. We don’t know what it will look like, but the expectation has been that it should seem familiar—everyone knows what a “MacBook” is supposed to look like—but thinner and lighter. In Mark Gurman’s latest Power On newsletter, he lets us know that last point will be especially true.
Gurman says the new OLED and touch MacBook Pro will be “significantly lighter” (emphasis his), with a lot of attention paid to redesigning the interior of the machine, minimizing and consolidating parts to make it lighter and easier to carry. The current 14-inch MacBook Pro is 25 percent heavier than the equivalent MacBook Air, at 3.4 pounds for the 14-inch model (compared to 2.7 pounds for the 13-inch Air). The larger 16-inch model is 4.7 pounds, compared to 3.3 pounds for the 15-inch Air. That’s a 42 percent weight difference.
It would hardly be cause for such emphasis on being dramatically lighter if Apple had achieved only a 10 percent weight reduction, and if it’s 20 percent lighter or more, it’s entering MacBook Air territory. We don’t yet know if the touchscreen MacBook will come in the same sizes or introduce a new sixe at, say 15 inches, but it’s safe to say it will be at least 14 inches. So a “significant” reduction in weight means it will almost certainly clock it at under three pounds, which will definitely be noticeable when carrying it in a bag.

title: iCloud+ custom emails limit raised from three to a more sane ten
content:
Apple has increased how many personalized email addresses you can make from custom domains connected to iCloud+, from a meager three up to a more useful ten.


iCloud
One of the features of iCloud+ is the ability to set up custom email domains with the service. Instead of using the old iCloud.com or mac.com addresses, users were able to connect domain names they owned and have custom emails instead.
On September 30, as first spotted on Reddit, an Apple Support page was quietly updated to reveal a change in usage limits for the feature. Now, users can set up to five custom domains with iCloud+, and create up to ten personalized email addresses per domain.

content:

PRICES CHECKED 6 OCTOBER 2026
As of October 2026, it’s an excellent time to buy a MacBook Air, although not as good as if you were buying before June 25 when Apple increased prices by $200/£200 for each model.
Apple refreshed the lineup in March 2026 with the new M5 chip. The current models are the best all-around laptop for most people, offering a good balance of price, portability, battery life, and performance.
Another update to the MacBook Air is not expected until 2027, so buyers can purchase now without worrying about an imminent refresh.
That said, whether you should buy now depends on your current device, budget, and what features matter most to you.


Buy a MacBook Air now if…
You’re upgrading from an Intel Mac: Apple’s transition away from Intel is accelerating, and support is shrinking.
You need a lightweight laptop: The 13-inch MacBook Air weighs just 2.7 pounds, making it ideal for travel, commuting, and working between locations.
You’re buying your first Mac: The MacBook Air is a user-friendly entry point to macOS. 
You need to: You need a laptop now: Your current device is broken, unreliable or no longer meets your needs.
You’re a student: The MacBook Air is one of the best student laptops thanks to its silent fanless design, long battery life, and portability.
You find a good deal: If you find the M5 MacBook Air with $100/£100 or more off grab it. During October Prime Day we saw $200 off selected models in the U.S. and savings of more than £150 in the U.K.
Don’t buy a MacBook Air now if…
You already own an M2, M3, or M4 MacBook Air: The M5 improvements are meaningful but not transformative for recent Apple Silicon owners.
You need power: Creative professionals should consider buying a MacBook Pro instead. The Air’s fanless design is excellent for silence and portability, but sustained workloads like 4K video exports or 3D rendering can cause thermal throttling.
You want a major redesign: OLED displays, ProMotion (120Hz), and thinner chassis redesigns are rumored for 2027.
You’re highly price-sensitive: It would be wise to wait for larger seasonal discounts if you can.
You’re interested in refurbished pricing: Apple Refurbished discounts are typically around 15%. If no M5 MacBook Air models are available, we recommend looking for a good deal on the M4 generation instead.





What’s the best MacBook Air price right now?
The M5 MacBook Air reached record-low prices at major retailers including Amazon and Walmart shortly after launch – something that’s unusual for a new Apple laptop. Discounts bringing the base model down to around $899/£989 ranked among the best deals we’ve seen.
Those prices are now much less likely to return. In June 2026, Apple increased MacBook Air prices by $200 across the range, making deep discounts harder to find.

Should you buy a MacBook Air during Prime Day or Black Friday?

				
					

				
			
Get a good deal on a MacBook Air

Foundry




If you are looking for discounts on new hardware, third-party resellers frequently offer deals throughout the year. Retailers such as Best Buy, Walmart, B&H Photo, and Costco frequently discount current and previous-generation Apple products. You may also see clearance deals after Apple launches new products as resellers clear out old stock.
Historically, prices may drop slightly further during:
Amazon Prime Day (June in 2026, usually July)
Black Friday / Cyber Monday (November)
October Prime Deal Days
Black Friday remains the strongest overall shopping period for MacBooks and Apple products do sell for less during major sales events, but:
The biggest discounts often apply to older or clearance models
Stock can be limited
Popular configurations sell out quickly
Savings may only be $50–$100 lower than today’s discounts.
If you need a laptop now, waiting probably isn’t necessary.






Is buying a refurbished MacBook Air smarter?
Buying a refurbished MacBook can be an excellent option – especially if you want to save money without sacrificing quality.
Apple Certified Refurbished Macs are usually around 15% cheaper than brand-new models and often visually indistinguishable from new products. Several factors make this a particularly compelling moment to buy a refurbished Mac, the main benefit being you can sidestep Apple’s price hikes while the Certified Refurbished Store is still selling models at the old, pre-hike prices.
Apple refurbished products include:
1-year warranty
Optional AppleCare
Full testing and inspection
New battery and outer shell when required
There are some risks of buying refurbished to consider, including: 
Stock availability is inconsistent
Desired colors/specs may not appear
Third-party refurbishers vary significantly in quality
Sometimes clearance sales on brand-new older models are actually cheaper
For most buyers, Apple Certified Refurbished is the safest refurbished option.





Best refurbished MacBook Air deal right now

Save up to $240 on the M5 MacBook Air
In the U.K. refurbished store you can choose between the M5 and M4 MacBook Air, including some very attractive prices for the older generation. 
Get a M4 MacBook Air for £849


Do you need to upgrade your current Mac?
You should upgrade immediately if your Mac is running on an Intel chip. If you still use an Intel-based Mac, upgrading is becoming increasingly urgent especially as Apple has confirmed that future versions of macOS will not support Intel.
Intel Macs also:
Offer far worse battery life
Run hotter and louder than Apple Silicon models
Lack modern features, such as Apple Intelligence
Lack support from developers
The most attractive reason to update is that a moving from Intel to Apple Silicon will feel like a generational leap rather than a normal upgrade.
See How long Macs & MacBooks last: Lifespan, support & when to upgrade for more information and read about macOS Golden Gate and Tahoe to find out what you are missing. 






Who should buy MacBook Air?
The MacBook Air is widely considered the best laptop for the majority of users due to its balance of portability, battery life, and performance. In our review of the MacBook Air M5 we said it delivers fantastic performance and is a winning formula that works just right for most users.
The MacBook Air is specifically recommended for the following groups:
General Students: It is the primary choice for those focused on writing, research, and productivity apps like Microsoft Office or Google Workspace.
Mobile Users and Travelers: Its lightweight design – under 3 pounds for the 13-inch model – makes it ideal for people constantly moving between classes, libraries, or cafes.
Office and Everyday Users: It is perfect for casual browsing, streaming, and standard office tasks.
Light Creatives: The 15-inch model is a strong fit for students or hobbyists engaged in light design, photo editing, or short video projects where professional-level sustained power isn’t required.
For more advice about which Mac to buy read Best Mac 2026: Every Apple Mac and MacBook compared and Which MacBook is best. 
Who shouldn’t buy MacBook Air 
While the MacBook Air is the right Mac for most students and general users, it is not the ideal choice for everyone. Certain professionals, high-end creatives, and budget-constrained buyers may find it unsuitable due to its thermal design, display limitations, and port selection. 
The most significant technical limitation of the MacBook Air is its fanless design that means it may throttle performance during long, intensive tasks like 4K video editing to keep temperatures optimal. If you have a demanding professional workload, perform sustained tasks like long video exports or 3D rendering, the MacBook Pro is the better choice. Note that a major upgrade for the MacBook Pro is expected in late 2026 or early 2027, potentially featuring OLED touchscreen displays and a slimmer design. See: Should you buy the MacBook Pro now or wait?
The Air is unsuitable for those who regularly perform:
Long video exports or 3D rendering: Performance can dip during sustained heavy workloads to maintain optimal temperatures.
Large-scale software development: Compiling massive codebases is better handled by the MacBook Pro’s active cooling.
AAA Gaming: While the M5 chip features enhanced ray-tracing, the lack of a fan causes performance to drop after approximately 10 minutes of intensive play.






What about the MacBook Neo?
Some of the traditional customers for the MacBook Air may want to consider the MacBook Neo that Apple introduced in March 2026. Starting at $699/£699 it lowered the starting price of a Mac laptop considerably. 
Because of its lower-cost, it may appeal to:
Casual users
Students on tight budgets
Buyers replacing Chromebooks or older Windows laptops
However, it includes compromises compared to the Air, including: 
Lower performance
Fewer premium features
Base models lack Touch ID and keyboard backlighting
For most users who can afford it, the MacBook Air remains the better long-term investment, but the Neo is certainly worth considering if you are looking for a low budget option.






Which are the best retailers to buy a Mac from?
Aside from Apple (View the MacBook Air in the Apple Store and View the MacBook Air in the Apple Store U.K). There are a number of third-party reseller that frequently discount the MacBook Air. 
When shopping at a reseller our advice is to always verify:
Processor generation 
RAM amount
SSD size
Whether the model is Intel or Apple Silicon
Don’t make the mistake of paying for a previous generation Mac without comparing it to the specs of the current model.

Verdict
The MacBook Air M5 is currently one of the easiest laptops to recommend. Apple addressed many long-standing complaints by increasing the base RAM and storage, while maintaining the Air’s excellent portability and battery life.
For most buyers:
Now is a safe time to buy
Discounts are already strong
Another refresh is unlikely until 2027
Waiting mainly makes sense if:
You already own a recent Apple Silicon Air
You want OLED or redesign changes
You’re holding out for major seasonal discounts
You want refurbished pricing on an M5 model

title: iPhone 13 Pro vs. iPhone 18 Pro Buyer's Guide: Is It Worth Upgrading?
content:
Apple released the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max in September 2026, five years after the iPhone 13 Pro and iPhone 13 Pro Max. The 2021 models introduced ProMotion displays, macro photography, a 3x Telephoto camera, and substantially longer battery life than their predecessors. They remain capable phones and support iOS 27, but owners now have five generations of upgrades to consider.


The iPhone 14 Pro brought the Dynamic Island, an Always-On display, a 48-megapixel Main camera, and Emergency SOS via satellite. The iPhone 15 Pro introduced the Action button and USB-C. The iPhone 16 Pro added larger displays, the Camera Control, a 48-megapixel Ultra Wide camera, and expanded video capabilities.

iPhone 17 Pro adopted an aluminum unibody with vapor chamber cooling and upgraded the Telephoto and front-facing cameras. This year's iPhone 18 Pro adds the A20 Pro chip, a variable-aperture Main camera, a smaller ‌Dynamic Island‌, and further gains in battery life and charging speed. For an iPhone 13 Pro owner, these changes accumulate across nearly every part of the phone.

starts at $1,199 and the Pro Max at $1,299, each with 256GB of storage. That is $200 more than the corresponding iPhone 13 Pro model's 2021 starting price, although the older phones started with 128GB. Apple no longer sells the iPhone 13 Pro, so anyone buying one now will be looking at a used or refurbished device. Here are the key differences:

Design and Display

Is It Worth Upgrading From an iPhone 13 Pro?

For most iPhone 13 Pro and iPhone 13 Pro Max owners ready to replace their phone, the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ is a very worthwhile upgrade. Five years of changes bring noticeable improvements to battery life, charging, outdoor display visibility, photography, and connectivity. The iPhone 13 Pro already has ProMotion and a capable three-camera system, but those strengths do not erase the breadth of the newer model's improvements.

Battery life may be the most immediate benefit, especially for an iPhone 13 Pro whose original battery has aged. Faster wired charging and USB-C also make the newer phone easier to live with, particularly if your other devices already use USB-C.

The camera upgrade is substantial across the whole system. All three rear cameras move from 12 to 48 megapixels, while the variable-aperture Main camera adds creative control and the Telephoto camera extends from 3x to 4x, with an additional optical-quality 8x option. The higher-resolution front camera, autofocus, and Center Stage are useful for group photos and video calls. Video creators gain considerably more through higher frame rates, improved Cinematic mode, external recording, and professional formats.

The A20 Pro and vapor chamber make the strongest performance case for demanding games, long recording sessions, and other sustained work. The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ also supports ‌Apple Intelligence‌, while the iPhone 13 Pro does not, even though both run ‌iOS 27‌.

The main physical trade-offs are size and weight: both ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ models are taller, thicker, and slightly heavier. Some users may find the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌'s aluminum chassis to be more vulnerable to dents and damage, even though the front and rear glass is stronger. U.S. buyers who rely on a physical SIM must also move to eSIM.

Apple raised iPad prices by $100–$200 in June, making today’s models more expensive than they were earlier this year. If you’re thinking about buying an iPad and want a good price, timing matters. If you’re looking for a bargain, the best opportunities to save are during sales events such as Amazon Prime Day and Black Friday. 
If you can’t wait – for example, because your current iPad no longer receives software updates, feels slow, has poor battery life, or doesn’t support Apple Intelligence – upgrading now may be the right choice. In that case, the safest models to buy are the iPad Air (M4) and iPad Pro (M5), as neither is expected to be replaced until 2027. By contrast, the iPad mini (A17 Pro) could be replaced as soon as October, while the entry-level iPad (A16) is expected later in 2026 or early 2027, so waiting is likely to pay off unless you find a substantial discount.
Before buying, consider whether you really need a Pro model, a cellular version, or even an iPad at all. If you’re looking for a laptop replacement, a MacBook Neo may offer better value. Buying refurbished is another smart way to save money, with Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store and reputable retailers offering lower prices while still providing a warranty and years of software support.
In this guide, we’ll explain the best and worst times to buy an iPad, which models are worth buying now, when the next updates are expected, and how to get the best value whether you’re buying new or refurbished. If you’re still deciding which iPad is right for you, see our complete iPad buying guide.

Should you buy an iPad now?
Two iPads are safe to buy without worrying about an imminent replacement: the iPad Air (M4) and iPad Pro (M5). Both were updated recently and aren’t expected to be refreshed until 2027.
The entry-level iPad (A16) and iPad mini (A17 Pro) are a different story. Both are widely expected to receive updates before the end of 2026, making them harder to recommend unless you find them at a significant discount.
Here’s our breakdown of the four types of iPad that Apple currently sells, and in each case whether you should buy now or wait.

For most people, it’s the best iPad Apple sells and is unlikely to be replaced until 2027, making now an excellent time to buy.

Should you buy? Yes
The iPad Pro (M5), launched in October 2025, remains Apple’s most capable tablet. It combines the M5 chip with a stunning Tandem OLED ProMotion display, support for up to 2TB of storage, and class-leading performance. The next update isn’t expected until 2027.
That said, it’s the right choice only if you’ll benefit from its extra power. Creative professionals working with demanding apps, large media projects, or intensive multitasking will appreciate what it offers. Most other buyers will find the iPad Air delivers a very similar everyday experience for considerably less money. Likewise, children and casual users are generally better served by the standard iPad or iPad mini than by Apple’s most expensive tablet.


When is the best time to buy an iPad

				
					

				
			
Foundry




The best time to buy an iPad is during major shopping events, particularly Black Friday and Amazon Prime Day, when retailers such as Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart typically offer their biggest discounts.
Black Friday and Cyber Monday (November/December)
Black Friday is usually the best time of the year to buy an iPad. In 2025, every current iPad model reached its lowest-ever price during the Black Friday sales, with discounts of up to $150. The entry-level iPad (A16), for example, fell to just $274.
If you can wait until November, Black Friday is your best opportunity to get the lowest prices on almost every iPad model. See Black Friday iPad deals.
Amazon Prime Day (June/July and October)
Amazon now holds two major Prime Day sales each year – one in June or July and another in October – and both regularly feature excellent iPad deals.
The June 2026 event was particularly significant because in the middle of the sale Apple increased iPad prices by $100 to $300, which made the discounts even larger.
The October Prime Day sale often matches or comes close to Black Friday discounts and is another excellent time to buy. See Prime Day iPad deals.
During Apple’s Back to School promotion
If you’re a student, teacher, or work in education, Apple’s Education Store offers year-round discounts on most iPads. During Apple’s annual Back to School promotion in the summer, eligible buyers also receive a free gift card, making it one of the best times to buy directly from Apple.
Note that the criteria are very strict for shopping in Apple’s Education Store. Customers need to verify their eligibility through UNiDAYS before accessing Education Store pricing.






When shouldn’t you buy an iPad?
The worst time to buy an iPad is just before Apple releases a new model. You’ll often end up paying full price for a device that’s about to be replaced, while retailers discount the outgoing model to clear stock.
The entry-level iPad (A16) and iPad mini (A17 Pro) fall into that category, with both expected to be refreshed before the end of 2026.
There are a few other situations where it’s worth thinking twice before buying:
If a major sale is just around the corner: If Amazon Prime Day or Black Friday is only a few weeks away, it’s usually worth waiting. These sales consistently offer the biggest iPad discounts of the year, often saving you $100 or more compared with buying at full price.
If you want a laptop replacement: An iPad can replace a laptop for some people, but it becomes much less compelling once you add accessories. A Magic Keyboard or similar case can add hundreds of dollars to the cost, bringing the total close to – or even above – the price of a MacBook. With the arrival of the $699 MacBook Neo, the value equation has shifted further. A similarly equipped iPad and keyboard can cost more while still being limited to iPadOS and mobile apps rather than full desktop software.
If you’re buying an older iPad: Discounts on older or refurbished iPads can be tempting, but always check how long they’ll continue to receive software updates. iPadOS 27 drops support for several older models, including the 2018 iPad Pro (3rd generation), 2019 iPad mini (5th generation) and 2020 iPad (8th generation). Buying an unsupported model means you’ll miss future features, security updates and, eventually, app compatibility.
If you want Apple Intelligence: Apple Intelligence isn’t available on every iPad. It requires an M1 chip or later (iPad Air and iPad Pro) or the A17 Pro chip in the current iPad mini. The entry-level iPad (A16) does not support Apple’s AI features, making it a less future-proof purchase.
If you don’t need cellular:  Think carefully before paying extra for a 5G cellular model. Cellular connectivity typically adds more than $100 to the purchase price, and you’ll usually need a separate data plan. If you already carry an iPhone, using Personal Hotspot is often a far cheaper alternative.
If fast wired transfers matter: Most people won’t notice USB speeds, but they matter if you regularly transfer large files via cable. The standard iPad is limited to USB 2.0 (480Mbps), the iPad mini supports 5Gbps, the iPad Air 10Gbps, while the iPad Pro offers Thunderbolt speeds of up to 40Gbps. 






What is the best iPad price right now?
Apple rarely discounts iPads. In fact, in June 2026, Apple increased iPad prices by $100 to $200, citing unprecedented component cost increases. The price rise came in the middle of Amazon’s Prime Day sale, during which we saw record-low prices. Prices that low are unlikely to return until a major sales event such as October Prime Day or Black Friday.

Other ways to save money when buying an iPad
If you’re flexible about where and when you buy, there are several ways to reduce the cost of a new iPad.
Buy a refurbished iPad: Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store is one of the best places to save money. Refurbished iPads undergo Apple’s full testing process, receive a new battery and outer shell where required, include the same one-year warranty as a new device, and are eligible for AppleCare+. Prices are typically around 15% lower than buying new, with savings of up to $450 on some iPad Pro models.
Use Apple’s Education Store: Students, teachers, and education staff can save 5–15% through Apple’s Education Store all year round. During Apple’s annual Back to School promotion, qualifying purchases also include a free gift, such as AirPods or an Apple Pencil. In the U.S., eligibility now needs to be verified through UNiDAYS before accessing Education Store pricing. Read: How to shop at Apple’s Education Store.
Trade in your old iPad: Apple’s Trade In programme can significantly reduce the cost of a new iPad. For the highest trade-in value, upgrade before Apple announces a replacement model, as trade-in prices typically fall once new devices are released.
Shop during major sales: The biggest discounts usually come from retailers such as Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart during Prime Day and Black Friday. Apple itself rarely discounts iPads, instead offering gift cards during promotions such as Black Friday and Back to School. While those offers can be worthwhile, third-party retailers almost always provide larger cash discounts.






Is buying a refurbished iPad a good idea?

				
					

				
			
Apple




Buying a refurbished iPad is one of the best ways to save money. You can often afford a model with more storage or even an iPad Pro for the price of a new entry-level iPad.
The key is to buy refurbished, not simply used. A properly refurbished iPad has been tested, repaired if necessary, and checked to ensure it works like new. A used iPad sold privately is typically sold “as is”, with no warranty, and could even be locked to the previous owner’s Apple ID.
Buy from Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store
The safest option is Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store. Every refurbished iPad is fully tested, fitted with a new battery and outer shell where required, cleaned, and repackaged with all original accessories. You also receive:
A one-year warranty, just like a new iPad.
The option to purchase AppleCare+.
Original accessories and packaging.
Prices are typically around 15% lower than buying new.
What to look for
If you’re buying from a third-party retailer, pay attention to a few key details:
Software support: Choose a model that will continue receiving iPadOS updates for several years. Older devices, such as the 2018 iPad Pro (3rd generation) and 2020 iPad (8th generation), no longer support iPadOS 27.
Storage: Aim for at least 128GB. Older 32GB and 64GB models can quickly run out of space with modern apps and games.
Condition: Check the retailer’s grading system so you know what cosmetic wear to expect.
Warranty: Buy from a seller that includes a warranty—ideally for at least one year.
Where to buy 
Apple Certified Refurbished: The safest choice, with the same warranty and support as a new iPad.
Reputable refurbishers: Retailers such as Back Market, Best Buy, and Amazon Renewed often offer deeper discounts, but always check the condition grading and warranty before buying.
If you buy from a trusted retailer and choose a model that still has years of software support ahead of it, a refurbished iPad can offer excellent value while saving you a significant amount of money.






Do you need to upgrade your current iPad?
Whether it’s time to replace your iPad depends on four things: software support, performance, battery life, and whether you’re missing features you actually want.
Your iPad no longer receives updates
The most important reason to upgrade is when your iPad stops receiving software and security updates. Apple typically provides major iPadOS updates for around six to eight years, with security updates often continuing for a while afterwards. See: How long does Apple support iPads?
As long as your iPad still receives security updates, it’s generally safe to keep using. Once those updates end, however, you’ll eventually lose app compatibility and expose yourself to increasing security risks.
As of 2026, iPads with an A14 chip or newer, or any M-series iPad, support iPadOS 27. Older models, including the 2018 iPad Pro and 2019 iPad Air, have reached the end of major software support.
It feels slow or the battery no longer lasts
Performance and battery life naturally decline with age. If apps take a long time to open, crash frequently, or the interface feels sluggish even after restarting, your iPad may be struggling to keep up. 
Which are the best retailers to buy an iPad from?
Aside from Apple (View the iPad in the Apple Store and View the iPad in the Apple Store U.K). There are a number of third-party resellers that frequently discount the different iPad models.

Similarly, if the battery no longer lasts through a typical day or the iPad shuts down unexpectedly, it may be time to replace the device – or at least the battery.
You want Apple Intelligence
One of the biggest reasons to upgrade today is Apple Intelligence. Apple’s AI features require an M-series chip or an A17 Pro processor.
If you own the current entry-level iPad (A16) or an older model, you won’t be able to use features such as Writing Tools, Priority Notifications, or Clean Up in Photos.
When you probably don’t need to upgrade
If your iPad still runs the latest version of iPadOS, performs well, and meets your needs, there’s little reason to replace it.
Owners of the M1 iPad Air or newer, as well as recent iPad Pro models, are unlikely to notice a dramatic difference in everyday tasks by upgrading to the latest generation. Unless you need a specific new feature or substantially more performance, you’re usually better off keeping your current iPad for another year or two.





Which iPad to choose

Commuters & travelersiPad mini (A17 Pro)The lightest iPad at just 293g. Its compact 8.3-inch screen is perfect for reading, note-taking, and slipping into a bag or large pocket.
Most people (all-rounder)iPad Air (M4)This is the best choice for the average user. It offers M4-level performance, a beautiful design, and a 13-inch option for those who want a large screen without paying Pro prices. When Apple introduces the new iPad this may change. 
Professionals & creativesiPad Pro (M5)The ultimate iPad with an M5 chip, Thunderbolt speeds up to 40Gbps, and a stunning display. If you’re a creative professional, the Pro is the iPad to get.

GamersiPad Pro (M5)The Pro’s 120Hz ProMotion display and M5 chip deliver the best gaming experience.

It’s generally a good time to buy a MacBook Pro. Apple refreshed the lineup in early 2026 with the M5 Pro and M5 Max models, and the next major chip upgrade isn’t expected until 2027, so the current machines should remain powerful and relevant for years. The main downside is price: Apple increased MacBook Pro prices by $300 to $500 in June 2026, making it more important than ever to shop around for discounts, consider Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store, or wait for major sales such as October Prime Day or Black Friday.
The only reason to delay your purchase is if you’re specifically interested in the rumoured MacBook Pro redesign could come in October 2026. Apple is widely expected to introduce its first touchscreen MacBook Pro, although current rumours suggest it could still use the existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, with the next major chip upgrade not arriving until 2027.
The MacBook Pro is best suited to creative professionals, software developers, engineers and other power users who need sustained performance, a premium display, plenty of ports and high memory configurations. If your workload consists mainly of web browsing, office work, studying or light creative tasks, the MacBook Air is likely to offer better value at a much lower price.
In this guide, we’ll explain whether you should buy now or wait, which MacBook Pro is right for you, the best times of year to buy, today’s best deals, and whether a refurbished model or MacBook Air might be a better choice.


Should you buy a MacBook Pro now? 
The MacBook Pro is the best MacBook Apple makes for users who need sustained performance, a premium display and professional features. While a new model with a touchscreen is rumored to launch soon, if you aren’t interested in a touchscreen, we still think it’s a good time to buy – provided you’re buying it for the right reasons.
Buy a MacBook Pro now if:
You’re upgrading from an Intel Mac: Apple is ending support for Intel Macs, so if you haven’t yet switched to Apple Silicon, now is a good time to do so. As Intel Macs reach the end of support, they’ll stop receiving security updates, leaving them vulnerable to newly discovered security flaws.
You need a new laptop: If your current Mac is broken, unreliable or slowing you down, there’s little reason to wait.
You edit video or create content: Whether you’re editing 4K video, working in Photoshop or Lightroom, producing music or creating 3D graphics, the MacBook Pro delivers the sustained performance creative professionals need.
You’re a software developer, engineer or AI professional: Compiling code, running virtual machines, working with AI models or processing large datasets is much faster on the MacBook Pro, particularly the M5 Pro and M5 Max models.
You need sustained performance: Unlike the fanless MacBook Air, the MacBook Pro uses active cooling to maintain peak performance during long exports, renders and other demanding workloads.
You need professional features: The MacBook Pro offers a Liquid Retina XDR display with ProMotion, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe charging and higher memory and storage options than the MacBook Air.
You find a good deal: Discounts of around $200/£200 or more are worth taking, especially during Prime Day or Black Friday sales.
You don’t want to wait for the next generation: The next major chip upgrade isn’t expected until 2027, so unless you’re specifically waiting for the rumoured touchscreen redesign, today’s MacBook Pro models should remain excellent choices for years.






When shouldn’t you buy a MacBook Pro?
The MacBook Pro is an excellent laptop, but it isn’t the right choice for everyone. If you don’t need its extra performance or professional features, you’ll save money – and probably be just as happy – with a MacBook Air. There are also a few situations where it’s worth waiting rather than buying today.
Don’t buy a MacBook Pro now if:
You already own a recent MacBook Pro: If you have an M2, M3 or M4 MacBook Pro, the performance improvements offered by the M5 generation are relatively modest.
You’re waiting for the redesign: Apple is widely expected to give the MacBook Pro its biggest redesign in years, with rumours pointing to an OLED touchscreen and a thinner, substantially lighter chassis.
You want the next-generation chips: Apple’s next high-end MacBook Pro processors should deliver another step up in performance and efficiency.
You’re looking for the best price: Apple raised MacBook Pro prices in June 2026, so today’s models are more expensive than ever. If you can wait, you’re likely to find better deals during October Prime Day or Black Friday, and prices could fall further once the next-generation models are announced.
You mainly use your laptop for everyday tasks: If your workload consists of web browsing, Microsoft Office, streaming, email, video calls or light photo editing, a MacBook Air offers excellent performance for much less money.
You’re a student with basic computing needs: If your coursework mainly involves writing essays, researching online or creating presentations, a MacBook Air is likely to be the better value.
Portability is your priority: The MacBook Air is thinner, lighter and completely silent thanks to its fanless design.
You’re on a budget: The MacBook Air delivers outstanding performance for most users while costing significantly less than the MacBook Pro.
For most people, the MacBook Air is the better buy. The MacBook Pro only comes into its own if you regularly run demanding professional workloads that benefit from its active cooling, more powerful chips, superior display, additional ports and higher memory options.

If you’re looking for the lowest price on a MacBook Pro, the best times to buy are during major sales events such as Amazon Prime Day in June/July or October and Black Friday.
Black Friday is typically the strongest shopping period for MacBook Pro deals, although the lowest prices are often reserved for older or clearance models, and popular configurations can sell out quickly.
Another time to look for deals is shortly after Apple launches a new model, as retailers often discount the previous generation to clear remaining stock, making it possible to save hundreds if you don’t need the latest chip.
If you’re a student, you can save all year. Students, teachers, and education staff can typically save $100 to $200 on a new MacBook Pro through Apple’s Education Store. However, the best time to buy is usually during Apple’s annual Back to School promotion in the summer, when qualifying customers can often claim a free pair of AirPods or another bonus gift alongside the education discount. Is buying a refurbished MacBook Pro a good idea?

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Buying a refurbished MacBook Pro can be a great way to save money – particularly if you buy directly from Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store.
As of July 2026, buying refurbished makes more sense than ever because Apple has continued to sell refurbished Macs at pre-price-hike prices, allowing buyers to avoid the $300 to $500 increases Apple introduced on new MacBook Pro models in June.
Apple Certified Refurbished Macs are typically around 15% cheaper than brand-new models and come with the same one-year warranty, 90 days of complimentary technical support, and the option to purchase AppleCare+. Every Mac undergoes extensive testing, is cleaned and inspected, and receives genuine Apple replacement parts where necessary.
The main downside is availability. Stock changes daily, so you may need to wait for the exact model, storage capacity, memory configuration, or colour you want. Newer MacBook Pro models also usually don’t appear in the refurbished store until several months after launch.
Third-party retailers, including Amazon, also sell refurbished Macs, but quality standards vary considerably. We generally recommend avoiding Macs that are more than five years old, as they may receive fewer years of macOS and security updates. In some cases, retailers also offer larger discounts on new, previous-generation MacBook Pro models during major sales events, so it’s always worth comparing prices before you buy.
For most buyers, Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store remains the safest and best-value way to buy a refurbished MacBook Pro.






Best refurbished MacBook Pro deal right now
Apple is selling the M5 MacBook Pro on its Certified Refurbished store in the U.S. for $300 off the full price. 
Get the MacBook Pro on Apple’s Refurbished Store.

Get the MacBook Pro on Apple’s Refurbished Store.



Which MacBook Pro to choose
Choose the M5 MacBook Pro if you want Pro features such as the better display, extra ports and active cooling, but don’t need the power of the M5 Pro or M5 Max.
Choose the M5 Pro MacBook Pro if you’re a professional who regularly edits 4K video, compiles large software projects, works with RAW photos, produces music or runs multiple demanding applications at once. For most creative professionals and developers, the M5 Pro offers the best balance of performance and price.
Choose the M5 Max MacBook Pro if your work pushes a laptop to its limits. The M5 Max is designed for users editing multiple streams of 8K video, creating complex 3D animations, running large AI or machine learning workloads, or handling visual effects and other GPU-intensive tasks. Unless you regularly perform these types of work, the M5 Pro is likely to offer better value. 






What about the MacBook Air?

				
					

				
			
The MacBook Air is a good alternative at a lower price.

Stephan Wiesend




If you’re considering a MacBook Pro, it’s also worth looking at the MacBook Air. Apple updated the Air in March 2026, and with a starting price of $1,299/£1,299 (the price increased by $200/£200 in June 2026), it’s significantly cheaper than the MacBook Pro.
The MacBook Air is a good choice if you:
Mainly browse the web, use Microsoft Office or stream media.
Are a student or home user with light computing needs.
Value portability and a silent, fanless design.
Want the best value MacBook.
However, the lower price comes with a few compromises. Compared to the MacBook Pro, the Air offers lower sustained performance, a less advanced display, fewer ports, and lower memory and storage limits.
Choose the MacBook Pro if you need:
Sustained performance for video editing, coding, 3D rendering or AI workloads.
A Liquid Retina XDR display with ProMotion and HDR.
More connectivity, including HDMI, an SDXC card slot and additional Thunderbolt ports.
Higher-end M5 Pro or M5 Max chips, with up to 128GB of unified memory.
For most everyday users, the MacBook Air is the better value. But if your work regularly pushes your laptop to its limits, the MacBook Pro is well worth the extra investment.






Do you need to upgrade your current Mac?

				
					

				
			
Apple




Whether you need to upgrade depends on three things: how old your Mac is, whether Apple still supports it, and whether it can keep up with the apps and features you use every day.
If you have an Intel Mac, it’s time to upgrade
With macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple has ended support for Intel Macs. While Apple is expected to continue providing security updates for the small number of Intel Macs that support macOS 26 Tahoe, that support is likely to last only another year or two.
The only Intel Macs that can run macOS Tahoe are:
16-inch MacBook Pro (2019)
13-inch MacBook Pro (2020, four Thunderbolt ports)
27-inch iMac (2020)
Mac Pro (2019)
If your Mac isn’t on this list, it may no longer receive the latest macOS updates and will eventually stop receiving security updates. For more advice, read How long Macs and MacBooks last: Lifespan, support and when to upgrade.
If you’re still using an Intel Mac, we recommend upgrading as soon as your budget allows. Moving from Intel to Apple Silicon is one of the biggest upgrades Apple has ever offered. You’ll benefit from dramatically faster performance, much longer battery life, quieter operation, Apple Intelligence support, and many more years of macOS compatibility. Read our guides to macOS Tahoe and macOS Golden Gate to see what you’ll gain by upgrading.






Which are the best retailers to buy a MacBook from?
Aside from Apple (View the MacBook Pro in the Apple Store and View the MacBook Pro in the Apple Store U.K). There are a number of third-party resellers that frequently discount the MacBook Pro.

Whether the model is Intel or Apple Silicon

Apple’s 2026 Watch lineup is now on sale, with the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 joining the Apple Watch SE 3. That makes this a reasonable time to buy if you want the latest features. If price matters more, compare the new models with discounted Series 11 and Ultra 3 stock – or wait for the October and Black Friday sales. The SE 3 remains the least expensive option in Apple’s current lineup, but it’s also the oldest as it was introduced in September 2025. 
If you don’t need a watch immediately, it’s worth considering the major sales events that follow Apple’s launch. Retailers consistently offer their biggest Apple Watch discounts during Amazon Prime Day (July and October) and Black Friday in November. During Prime Day in June 2026, for example, we saw discounts ranging from $50 to $120 on current models.
In this guide, we’ll explain whether you should buy an Apple Watch now or wait, the best times of year to find the biggest discounts, and how to avoid paying full price just before a new model arrives. Read our Macworld’s Best Apple Watch guide for more buying advice. 
Should I buy an Apple Watch now? At a glance

Buy an Apple Watch now if…

				
					

				
			
Mahmoud Itani / Foundry




The Series 12 and Ultra 4 are now on sale alongside the SE 3 and there are no new models expected. Buy now if you need a watch soon or the model you want meets your needs at a price you’re happy to pay. The Series 12 is the best everyday choice, the SE 3 is the best value, and the Ultra 4 makes sense if you need its longer battery life or outdoor features. A discounted Series 11 or Ultra 3 could also be worth buying if you don’t need the latest additions.
You should consider buying now if:
Your current Apple Watch cannot run watchOS 27, or its battery no longer lasts long enough for your needs.
You’re buying your first Apple Watch or upgrading from a much older model. The current watches offer substantial improvements in displays, performance, health tracking and battery life.
You want the Series 12 or Ultra 4’s new Health Sensing System, more frequent heart-rate and HRV readings, and Readiness score. Live Rewind and Siri Recap are due in beta later in 2026, so don’t count on using those immediately.
You would benefit from the Ultra 4’s up to 50-hour battery life, satellite communication or specialist outdoor features.
You need a watch before a trip or event, or you find a worthwhile discount on a model that suits you.






Don’t buy an Apple Watch now if…
The main reason to wait now is price: retailers may discount the new models during October sales and Black Friday.
You may want to wait or choose a different model if:
You want the lowest possible price and are happy to wait for the next major sale. Compare any Series 12 or Ultra 4 offer with remaining Series 11 and Ultra 3 stock.
You already own a Series 10 or 11 and do not need the Series 12’s new health sensing features. Its quoted everyday battery life remains 24 hours.
You own an Ultra 3 and its 42-hour battery life and outdoor features already meet your needs. The Ultra 4’s 50-hour rating is its clearest reason to upgrade.
You are considering a used watch that cannot run watchOS 27. The Series 8, SE 2 and original Ultra, along with older models, miss out on the latest major software update.
You use an Android phone. Apple Watch requires an iPhone.

Our verdict: This is the Apple Watch we’d recommend to most people buying a new watch today. Its new health sensing features make it a more substantial upgrade than the Series 11 was, while the starting price has stayed the same. Owners of recent watches should weigh those additions against the cost: a discounted Series 11 – or keeping the watch they already have – may be the better value.

The Apple Watch SE 3 is the best-value Apple Watch in the lineup and the model we’d recommend for most iPhone users. Announced in September 2025, it brought many features that were previously reserved for Apple’s premium watches, including an always-on display, temperature sensing, fast charging and the S10 chip used in the Series 11 and Ultra 3.
If you don’t need Apple’s most advanced health sensors, the SE 3 delivers almost everything that makes the Apple Watch great at a much lower price. It starts at $249 / £219, although we’ve already seen it discounted to $199 during major sales.
The SE 3 also supports Siri AI in watchOS 27 when paired with a compatible Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone. Siri AI is currently in beta and rolling out in English. The SE 3 does not support the separate Audio Intelligence features coming to the Series 12 and Ultra 4, including Live Rewind and Siri Recap.
Buy the Apple Watch SE 3 if:
You want the best-value Apple Watch.
You’re buying your first smartwatch.
You mainly want fitness tracking, notifications and Apple’s core smartwatch features.
You want safety features such as Fall Detection, Crash Detection and heart-rate alerts.
You’re buying for a child or older family member, particularly the cellular model.
Don’t buy the Apple Watch SE 3 if:
You need ECG or blood oxygen monitoring, which are only available on the Series 12 and Ultra 4.
You want the brightest display and most premium design—the SE 3 still has thicker bezels than the flagship models.
You need longer battery life. The SE 3 is rated for 18 hours, compared with 24 hours for the Series 12.
You’re happy to spend more for Apple’s most advanced health and fitness features.
Our verdict: The Apple Watch SE 3 is an outstanding budget smartwatch. Its always-on display, S10 processor, fast charging and improved health features make it a huge step up from the SE 2. Unless you specifically need ECG, blood oxygen monitoring or the longer battery life of the Series 11, the SE 3 is the Apple Watch we’d recommend to most buyers.

The Apple Watch Ultra 4 is Apple’s most capable watch, aimed at endurance athletes, hikers, divers and anyone who regularly spends more than a day away from a charger. It starts at $799/£749, the same starting price as the Ultra 3, and retains the 49mm titanium case, bright display, dual-frequency GPS, satellite communication and diving support. 
Battery life is the strongest reason to choose the new model. Apple rates the Ultra 4 for up to 50 hours of normal use, up from 42 hours on Ultra 3, or 84 hours in Low Power Mode, up from 72. Its new Extended Workout modes can track outdoor activity for up to 25 hours with full GPS and heart-rate readings, or up to 45 hours in Max Extended Workout mode. Like the Series 12, it gains the new Health Sensing System, more frequent heart-rate and HRV readings, and a Readiness score. Its S11 chip supports Audio Intelligence, although Live Rewind and Siri Recap are due in beta later in 2026. 
Buy the Apple Watch Ultra 4 if:
You want the longest battery life available on an Apple Watch, particularly for travel, long shifts or time away from a charger.
You need extended outdoor workout tracking, precision dual-frequency GPS or satellite communication.
You hike, dive or take part in endurance sports and will use its rugged case, Action button and specialist features.
You want the new Health Sensing System in an Ultra watch and are upgrading from a substantially older model.
Don’t buy the Apple Watch Ultra 4 if:
You already own an Ultra 3 and its 42-hour battery life meets your needs. It retains many of the same outdoor features, including satellite communication and dual-frequency GPS.
You find an Ultra 3 at a substantial discount and do not need the Ultra 4’s longer battery life, new health sensing or extended workout modes.
You mainly want advanced health features in an everyday watch. The smaller Series 12 has the same new Health Sensing System and S11 chip for half the starting price.
You prefer a smaller or lighter watch. The Ultra 4’s 49mm case can feel bulky, especially for sleep tracking.
Our verdict: The Ultra 4 is worth buying if you will benefit from its 50-hour battery life, extended workout tracking or outdoor safety features. It also offers the Series 12’s new health sensing in a more rugged watch. For everyday use, the Series 12 offers better value; if you already own an Ultra 3, compare the cost of upgrading with how much its extra eight hours of rated battery life and new health features matter to you. 


Should I buy an older Apple Watch?

				
					

				
			
Foundry




The Series 11 and Ultra 3 are now the previous-generation models and may be good buys if retailers discount them enough. Before choosing any older Apple Watch, check both its price against the current model and whether it can run watchOS 27. The Series 9 and Ultra 2 are the oldest supported Apple Watch models models in their respective ranges; the SE 3 is the only supported SE.
The following models cannot install watchOS 27, so we would generally avoid buying them unless the price is exceptionally low and you are comfortable using older software:
Apple Watch Series 6 (2020)
Apple Watch Series 7 (2021)
Apple Watch Series 8 (2022)
Apple Watch SE (2nd generation, 2022)
Apple Watch Ultra (1st generation, 2022)
Start by comparing a discounted Series 11 with the Series 12, or an Ultra 3 with the Ultra 4. The Series 11 retains the Series 12’s 24-hour everyday battery rating but lacks its new Health Sensing System and Audio Intelligence features. The Ultra 3 retains satellite communication and dual-frequency GPS, but its rated battery life is 42 hours rather than the Ultra 4’s 50 hours. Series 10 and Ultra 2 can offer further savings if their price and battery condition make sense; Series 9 is the oldest standard model that runs watchOS 27.
What to look for when buying an older Apple Watch
Choose an S9 chip or newer for the longest software support.
Buy refurbished if possible. Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store includes a one-year warranty, while reputable third-party refurbishers can also offer good value.
Shop during major sales. Previous-generation Apple Watches often receive their biggest discounts during Prime Day and Black Friday.
Check the battery and Activation Lock. If you’re buying used, confirm the battery is in good condition, inspect the watch for damage, and make sure Activation Lock has been removed before you buy.

When is the best time to buy an Apple Watch?
The best time to buy an Apple Watch depends on whether you want the newest model or the lowest price.
The Series 12 and Ultra 4 are now on sale, alongside the SE 3. If you want the latest model and are happy with its price, you can buy now without an imminent replacement to worry about. If getting a discount matters more, compare retailers during the expected October sales and Black Friday in November.
The September launch also makes the Series 11 and Ultra 3 worth checking. Retailers may reduce remaining stock, but compare the actual saving with the features you would give up: the Series 12 and Ultra 4 add new health sensing, while the Ultra 4 also increases rated battery life from 42 to 50 hours.
Apple kept the new models’ starting prices at $399/£369 for Series 12 and $799/£749 for Ultra 4. Individual configurations and retailer prices vary.






When shouldn’t you buy an Apple Watch?
Avoid buying an Apple Watch:
Just before Apple’s annual September event, unless you need one immediately.
At full price when a major sale is only days away, such as Prime Day or Black Friday.
Without comparing prices. Check multiple retailers and use price-tracking tools such as CamelCamelCamel to avoid inflated “sale” prices.
If you’re paying extra for cellular but don’t need it. Cellular Apple Watch typically cost around $100 more and require a monthly data plan, while the GPS model offers better value for most people.
If battery life is your top priority. Apple Watch battery life still trails some competing smartwatches, so you may prefer an alternative platform if multi-day battery life is essential.

Where to find the best Apple Watch deals

Apple rarely discounts the Apple Watch itself, so the best deals are usually found at third-party retailers – we check these every month and record the best deals here: Top Apple Watch discounts & deals – Big savings on all models.
Best places to buy: Amazon is consistently one of the best places to find Apple Watch discounts, particularly during major sales. Other good options in the U.S. include Best Buy, Walmart, Target and Costco. In the U.K., check Amazon, Currys, Argos, John Lewis and KRCS.
Shop during major sales: The biggest discounts typically arrive during Amazon Prime Day (July and October) and Black Friday/Cyber Monday (November). Savings of $100–$150 on current-generation models are common. During Prime Day 2026, for example, the Apple Watch Series 11 fell to $279 ($120 off) and the Ultra 3 dropped to $649 ($150 off).
Check for education discounts: Students, teachers and education staff may qualify for discounted Apple Watch pricing through Apple’s Education Store U.S. (and Education Store U.K.). For more information read our guide to how to get a student discount at the Apple Education Store.
Tip: Before buying, compare prices across several retailers and check the recent price history with a tool such as CamelCamelCamel to make sure you’re getting a genuine deal rather than a temporary “discount” from an inflated price.






Is it worth buying a refurbished Apple Watch?
Buying a refurbished Apple Watch is another great way to save money, provided you buy from a reputable seller and choose a model that will continue to receive software updates.
Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store is the safest option. Every watch undergoes rigorous testing, cleaning and inspection, comes with a one-year warranty, includes new accessories, and is eligible for AppleCare. Apart from the plain white box, it’s difficult to tell the difference between a refurbished Apple Watch and a brand-new one. You can typically save around 15% on recent models, with even bigger discounts on older generations.
Check Apple’s U.S. Refurbished Store or U.K. Refurbished Store for current models, configurations and prices. Stock changes regularly; compare any refurbished Series 11 or Ultra 3 with the price of a new Series 12 or Ultra 4 before buying.
The best Apple Watch refurbished deals: 
Apple’s U.S. Refurbished Store often has Apple Watch Series 11, 10 and 9, SE 3, SE 2, Ultra 2 and Ultra 3.
Get a refurbished Apple Watch Series 11 for $339, $60 off
You may also find the Apple Watch Series 11, 10 and 9, SE 2, SE 3 and Ultra 3 at Apple’s U.K. Refurbished Store. 
Get a refurbished Apple Watch Series 11 for £309, £60 off
Third-party refurbishers can also offer excellent value, but quality varies. Terms such as “Excellent” or “Grade A”aren’t standardised, so always check the seller’s warranty, return policy and battery condition before buying. Be aware that Amazon Renewed devices, for example, aren’t refurbished to Apple’s standards and may not include a new battery or replacement parts.
The other key consideration is software support. Older Apple Watches eventually stop receiving new versions of watchOS, so avoid buying a model that’s nearing the end of its supported life. For the best balance of price and features, compare refurbished Series 11 and Ultra 3 models with the new generation first. Series 9, Series 10 and Ultra 2 can cost less and still run watchOS 27, but check their condition and savings carefully.
A refurbished Apple Watch can be one of the best values in Apple’s lineup – as long as you buy from a trusted seller and don’t choose a model that’s too old.
Read: Should I buy a refurbished Apple Watch? for more information.






 FAQ 


1.
Should I wait for the next Apple Watch?
You do not need to wait for 2026’s launch: the Series 12 and Ultra 4 went on sale in September 2026, and the SE 3 remains in Apple’s lineup. If you need a watch now, choose the model that fits your needs and budget. If you are mainly looking for a lower price, consider waiting for a sale or comparing discounted Series 11 and Ultra 3 stock. 
Apple has not announced when the next Apple Watch models will arrive, but we expect that the next update will happen in September 2027.





2.
How long does Apple support an Apple Watch?
Apple has traditionally supported Apple Watches with major watchOS updates for around five to six years, but that changed with watchOS 27, announced at WWDC 2026.
Apple dropped support for five older models in a single release:
Apple Watch Series 6 (2020)
Apple Watch Series 7 (2021)
Apple Watch Series 8 (2022)
Apple Watch SE (2nd generation, 2022)
Apple Watch Ultra (1st generation, 2022)
As a result, watchOS 27 only supports Apple Watches with an S9 chip or later, starting with the Apple Watch Series 9. While Apple may continue to provide security updates for older models for a limited time, they no longer receive new watchOS features.
The change makes software support a much more important consideration when buying an older or refurbished Apple Watch. If you want the longest possible lifespan, choose a model with an S9 chip or newer.





3.
Is the Apple Watch Series 11 still worth buying?
If it is substantially cheaper than the Series 12. Both have up to 24 hours of rated everyday battery life, but the Series 12 adds more frequent heart-rate and HRV measurements, a Readiness score and support for upcoming Audio Intelligence features, so be sure that you are willing to give those features up for the saving.

Apple rarely discounts its own products. Even during its annual Black Friday shopping event, which runs from Black Friday to Cyber Monday, Apple typically offers gift cards with eligible purchases instead of cutting prices.

 FAQ 


1.
When are the best Apple deals? 
Apple deals are generally best during major retail events like Black Friday and Amazon Prime Day, or specifically for students during Apple’s annual “Back to School” promotion. While Apple itself rarely offers direct price cuts on new hardware, third-party resellers frequently discount products throughout the year.
The optimal time to buy depends heavily on the product’s release cycle and the specific retailer, though: 
iPhones: The best time to buy is often in the spring or summer, several months after the September launch, when third-party resellers begin offering deeper discounts . Conversely, the worst time is August, just before new models arrive and trigger price drops on older generations.
Macs and iPads: These see significant discounts during Black Friday (late November) and Amazon Prime Day (typically July and October). For students, the Back to School event (running June–September in the U.S. and July–October in the U.K.) is ideal, as Apple often bundles free accessories like AirPods or Apple Pencils with purchases.
Apple Watch: Major savings are typically found during Black Friday and Prime Day events.





2.
Are Apple refurbished deals worth it?
Apple refurbished deals are widely considered worth it, particularly when purchasing directly from the official Apple Refurbished Store, where products are restored to a “like-new” condition. While third-party resellers often provide steeper discounts, Apple’s own process is uniquely rigorous, offering a balance of significant savings and the same protections as a brand-new purchase. 
Buying directly from Apple is often described as “almost indistinguishable” from buying new. According to our guide How much can you save at Apple’s Refurbished Store?, the company puts every device through a “stringent refurbishment process” that includes full functional testing, thorough cleaning, and inspection.
Key benefits of the official Apple Refurbished Store include:
Hardware Replacements: Refurbished iPads and iPhones receive a brand-new battery and outer shell .
Warranty and Support: All products come with a standard one-year limited warranty, 90 days of technical support, and are eligible for AppleCare .
Full Accessories: Devices are repackaged in a plain white box with all original manuals and cables .
Savings: You can typically save around 15% off the retail price for recent models, with much higher discounts on older generations.
Avoid the Apple price hikes: Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store sells products at the old, pre-hike prices – meaning you can effectively sidestep the recent price increases entirely. 





3.
Is it better to buy Apple products from Amazon or Apple?
Deciding whether to buy Apple products from Amazon or directly from Apple depends on whether you prioritize immediate cost savings or the specific perks and guarantees offered by the manufacturer. While Amazon often provides deeper discounts, Apple offers unique benefits like trade-in credits, education pricing, and the assurance of receiving the latest models.





4.
Does Apple ever discount products directly?
Apple rarely provides direct price reductions on its new products, preferring to maintain steady Old MSRP pricing throughout a product’s lifecycle. Instead of traditional discounts, the company typically utilizes alternative methods to provide value directly to consumers, such as gift card incentives during major shopping events, education pricing, and a dedicated refurbished store. 
While you will not often see a lower price tag on a new iPhone or Mac at the Apple Store, the company does offer several ways to save:
Apple Shopping Events: During events like Black Friday and Cyber Monday, Apple typically offers gift cards rather than price cuts. For example, in the 2025 holiday season, Apple provided gift cards ranging from $25 to $250 for eligible purchases.
Education Store: Students, teachers, and higher education staff can access year-round discounts on Macs and iPads . During the annual “Back to School” event, Apple often includes a “freebie” like AirPods or an Apple Pencil with qualifying purchases.
Apple Refurbished Store: This is the primary way to get a direct price reduction from Apple. Products are fully reconditioned, come with a one-year warranty, and can be discounted by hundreds of dollars or pounds.
Trade-In Program: Apple allows customers to trade in old devices to receive credit toward a new purchase, effectively lowering the out-of-pocket cost.
