title: Best magnetic power banks and MagSafe portable chargers for iPhone 2026
content:
Macworld





Portable power banks that charge your phone are popular, but wireless battery packs using Apple’s magnetic MagSafe technology offer a simpler and smarter cable-free solution for iPhone 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18 and Air users.
Phone batteries are prone to run dry just when you’re heading away from a power source, so having a portable charging source is one of today’s necessities. Annoyingly, most power banks require you to carry around a cable, too. Wireless power banks do away with cables but come with their own major limitation—the inefficiency of wireless charging means you need a high-capacity power bank to fully charge a drained iPhone.
MagSafe is a technology that’s compatible with all iPhone 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, Air and Duo models, from the mini to the Pro Max, but strangely missing from the 16e model. It allows accessories to clamp magnetically to the back of the iPhone, making the charging connection more efficient. We haven’t yet had an iPhone Duo in for testing with these magnetic power banks, but the new folding iPhone is MagSafe friendly.
We put the best portable chargers through a series of rigorous iPhone recharging tests, and have listed the winners by power, portability and functionality:
Best high-capacity 10k MagSafe power banks
Best small portable 5K magnetic power banks
Best multi-device charging MagSafe power banks 
Best capacity magnetic power bank for you
You should consider size when it comes to a power bank: physical size and battery capacity. The higher the battery capacity, the more recharging power you’ll get from the power bank—but you’ll also be carrying around a larger, heavier item. Lighter, slimmer power banks are easier to pocket even when clamped to your phone. Larger power banks might not fit in your trouser pocket and can slide off easier when pocketed even if clamped magnetically.
10K power banks (with a 10000mAh battery capacity) can charge a phone close to two times over, while 5K (5000mAh) battery packs usually stretch between 60-75%, which is often enough to get you to the next wall-socket powering opportunity. If you are relying on the power bank for long-haul travel or a camping trip, a 10K battery or higher will suit you better. Belkin even offers a mid-range 8K power bank.
Milliamp hours (mAh) is quite a blunt measurement of battery capacity. It’s great for quickly differentiating between power bank sizes but we also list the capacity in the more accurate watt hours (Wh).
Also, look out for power banks that are built using the latest semi-solid-state battery technology that uses less liquid electrolyte than standard litium-ion power banks, making them more durable, longer lasting, and safer.
Wireless power bank charging speed
Wireless charging speeds vary from 7.5W (MagSafe Compatible) to 15W (certified MagSafe and Qi2), all the way to the very fastest wireless charging at 25W (Qi2.2). While it’s not as efficient as using a cable to charge a phone, magnetic wireless charging is a step closer to doing away with cables altogether. Qi2 25W brings wireless charging close to wired speed but only iPhones 16 and later support that speed, and some power banks include a built-in USB-C cable for even faster charging up to 45W. The iPhone Air can manage 20W max on even a 25W charger. See Which wireless tech is best for your iPhone?.

How we tested
MagSafe charger testing was conducted using an iPhone 13 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro and 16 Pro, subscribed to a 5G network and WiFi, with screen off and all default settings.
Our test is a simple battery recharge shootout. We let our test-unit iPhone Pro (3095mAh battery capacity) drain to just 10% and then set the Battery Pack to work recharging the phone. We then assigned the charger a score of whatever percentage it managed to charge the iPhone to and subtract the 10%; we test each model at least twice.
It’s not a real-world test of day-to-day use where you’ll likely be using your phone for various tasks (of varying battery usage) and in different environmental conditions and network configurations. But it does give us a common score format that we can use to compare different battery-pack models.

				
					

				
			
Why is magnetic wireless better?
The MagSafe connection to Apple’s iPhone is precise enough to make wireless charging more efficient as around 20% of non-magnetic power loss is from poor placement of a phone and the wireless charging pad. Standard Qi wireless charging can lose as much as 50% of the portable battery’s power, but MagSafe and Qi2 wireless charging loses ‘just’ 30%. Hot out of the gadget laboratory, the new Qi 2.2 (also known as Qi2 25W) brings even faster 25W wireless charging for the iPhone 16, 17 and 18. 15% will be plenty fast enough for most of us but who doesn’t want the fastest possible charging when your iPhone’s battery icon is in the red?
Why comparing Watt Hours is better than Milliamp Hours
Phone batteries are generally rated in Milliamp Hours (mAh) but this is a measure of electrical charge, while a Watt Hour is equal to one watt of energy consumed for one hour of time.
When comparing battery capacities and how much a power pack will boost a phone’s internal battery, energy is more important than electrical charge.
And mAh ignores a battery voltage, which determines the wattage (power) of a battery.
If the mAh is the same, the higher the voltage, the greater the actual stored power.
For example, Apple’s MagSafe Battery Pack is rated at just 1460mAh but it has a higher voltage potential (7.62V) than the iPhone (3.81V) or other battery packs, meaning that it can provide more power to an iPhone than its mAh suggests; in fact, it is actually 2920mAh.
To go into further depth about this read our feature iPhone battery capacities compared that also lists all iPhones battery life in mAh and Wh.
Anatomy of a magnetic power bank

				
					

				
			
TORRAS




A lot more than a battery goes into the making of a magnetic power bank.
Of course, the battery is the most important component, but the wireless charging coils and magnetic connection are vital for efficient and therefore fast and powerful charging. The transmitter coil transfers power by electromagnetic induction.
The magnets need to be set up to exactly connect the transmitting coils—here on the power bank— to the receiving coils, in this case inside the iPhone.
The example shown above is the Torras MagStall Wireless Power Bank, reviewed in our chart. You can see the various parts, including that power bank’s rotating stand/handle.
Which magnetic wireless tech is right for each iPhone?
iPhone 7 and earlier: Don’t support wireless charging. 
iPhone 8 – iPhone X/XS/XR: Support wireless charging. iPhone 8 and later can charge wirelessly at 7.5W but on a less efficient non-magnetic Qi pad.
iPhone 11 and earlier: Don’t support MagSafe. iPhone 8 and later can charge wirelessly but on a less efficient non-magnetic Qi pad.
iPhone 12 – iPhone 15: Support MagSafe and Qi2. Can wirelessly charge at 7.5W with “MagSafe-Compatible” power banks and chargers, and at 15W with certified MagSafe or Qi2 power banks and chargers.
iPhone 16 – iPhone 18: Support MagSafe, Qi2 and Qi2.2. Can wirelessly charge at 7.5W with “MagSafe-Compatible” power banks and chargers, at 15W with certified MagSafe or Qi2 power banks and chargers, and at 25W with Qi2.2-certified power banks and chargers.
Is charging via a cable faster or safer than magnetic wireless charging?
Charging via a cable is nearly always faster than wireless, even the latest Qi2.2 wireless chargers. Wireless charging is inefficient, losing some of its energy transfer through heat, for example. MagSafe, Qi2, and Qi2.2 magnetic connections dramatically improve efficiency but sticking a cable in is still a faster method, if not as convenient.
Most magnetic wireless power banks include at least one USB-C port, and some even include a port and an integrated cable for ultimate convenience. Models after the iPhone 17 can charge to 50% in 20 minutes or under via a cable and a 45W or higher charger or power bank. But wireless is so simple and cable-free that we don’t mind waiting an extra 15 minutes or so to reach such a charge wirelessly.
Why does my phone occasionally charge slowly or even stop charging?
This phone charging behavior is due to the built-in battery management feature on your iPhone. A phone heats up during charging as power is exchanged between the charger’s coils and the iPhone’s own. The phone actively adjust its charging behavior accordingly. This can slow down or temporarily pause charging to protect battery health and extend its lifespan. This is completely normal. Once the phone cools down, charging will automatically resume as normal.
What is a semi solid state battery?
The material that carries ions back and forth inside a battery is called “electrolyte”. Traditional lithium-ion batteries use a volatile, free-flowing liquid for electrolyte. As their name suggests, solid-state batteries use a solid material such as a ceramic or polymer. But semi-solid-state batteries are more common in today’s new generation of power banks.
A semi-solid-state battery uses a mix of solid particles in a much smaller amount of liquid, making a hybrid thick gel, paste or slurry. By reducing the liquid content to a minimum, semi-solid-state batteries increase stability and durability and significantly lower the risk of leaks, fires, and dangerous thermal runaway.
What about non-wireless power banks?
Wireless charging—especially magnetic wireless charging—is super convenient and does away with the need to carry around messy cables to connect your device to the battery pack.
But wired charging is nearly always faster and not much of an inconvenience if you are not out and about. Over on our sister site Tech Advisor I have reviewed the best power banks that includes standard non-wireless battery packs that might be a decent solution as well as the power banks reviewed above.
Do magnetic power banks work when the iPhone is in a case?
Yes, most quality iPhone cases are compatible with MagSafe having their own magnet ring to ensure a close connection between the power bank’s magnetic charging coils and the iPhone’s own. You can find exactly which are supported in our roundups of the best iPhone 17 cases, best iPhone 16 cases and best iPhone 15 cases.

Which iPad should you buy? 

				
					

				
			
There’s an iPad for everyone.

Foundry




iPad: The budget recommendation
The standard iPad is the best choice if price is your priority. It’s powerful enough for everyday tasks, streaming, schoolwork and casual gaming, but it’s the only current iPad that doesn’t support Apple Intelligence. With a replacement expected in early 2027, we’d look for a substantial Prime Day discount.
iPad mini: Best for portability 
The iPad mini is the best choice if you want maximum portability, but we’d be cautious about buying one this Prime Day. A new model could arrive later in October, with an OLED display among the expected upgrades. Only buy the current model if the discount is good enough to compensate.
iPad Air: Best choice for most buyers
The M4 iPad Air is the best choice for most people and probably the safest Prime Day buy. It offers considerably more performance than the standard iPad without the expense of the Pro, comes in 11-inch and 13-inch sizes, and isn’t expected to be replaced until 2027.
iPad Pro: Best for professionals/creative users
The M5 iPad Pro is aimed at demanding creative and professional users who will benefit from its performance and OLED display. It’s also safe to buy this Prime Day, but most people will get better value from the iPad Air.
For more advice read our guide to the Best iPad.


						

							


Prime Day iPad deals to avoid

				
					

				
			
Dominik Tomaszewski / Foundry




When deciding whether to shop for an iPad deal, we recommend you keep a few things in mind:
If you’re considering an iPad as a laptop replacement, remember to factor in the price of a keyboard. Adding an Apple keyboard case can add hundreds to the cost and, depending on the iPad, push the total close to or above the price of a MacBook. The arrival of the lower-cost MacBook Neo makes that comparison even more important.
Be particularly cautious about iPad mini deals. The current A17 Pro model could be replaced as soon as later in October, with an OLED display among the expected upgrades. Unless the Prime Day discount is substantial, you may be better off waiting.
The iPad (A16) is currently the only tablet in Apple’s active lineup that does not support Apple Intelligence. A replacement is expected in early 2027, so avoid paying close to Apple’s full price. A substantial discount, however, can still make the current model a good-value choice.
Deals on older or refurbished iPads can be tempting, but check software support before buying. iPadOS 27 drops support for several older models, so make sure the iPad you’re considering can run the current operating system.
Avoid paying extra for a Cellular model unless you truly need it. Cellular versions cost significantly more and may also require a monthly data plan. If you usually carry an iPhone, Personal Hotspot is often a cheaper alternative.
Casual users should also think twice before jumping on an iPad Pro (M5) deal. Unless you need its OLED display or additional performance for demanding creative and professional workflows, the M4 iPad Air offers better value for most people.
Likewise, don’t pay extra for the iPad Pro’s nano-texture glass unless you regularly work in bright or uncontrolled lighting.


						

							


Should you buy an iPad during Prime Day?
October Prime Day is one of the better times of the year to buy an iPad, particularly after Apple raised iPad prices substantially in June. Amazon’s October sale often comes close to Black Friday pricing, so a good deal could offset much of Apple’s price increase. 
The model you choose matters, though. The M4 iPad Air and M5 iPad Pro are relatively safe buys because neither is expected to be replaced until 2027. The A16 iPad can also be worth buying at a substantial discount, although it is the only current iPad without Apple Intelligence. We’d be much more cautious about the iPad mini, as a new model could arrive soon after Prime Day.
There are a few other things to consider before making a purchase:
Prime membership is required: Many of the best deals are exclusive to Amazon Prime members. If you’re not already subscribed, you might be able to take advantage of Amazon’s 30-day free trial or you could sign up for a month and cancel afterward. As well as getting free two-day shipping, Prime customers also get access to Prime Video and Music. Prime memberships cost $139 / £95 annually, or $14.99 / £8.99 / AU$6.99 every month. 
Other sales: If you miss Prime Day, you’ll have another chance to save during the Black Friday sales in November which historically brings some of the lowest iPad prices of the year.
Student Discounts: Students can save significantly through the Apple Education Store. For example, students can save $50/£50 on the iPad Air and $100/£100 on the iPad Pro when shopping at Apple’s U.S. Education Store or Apple’s U.K. Education Store.
Compare Prices: Amazon isn’t always the cheapest option. Retailers such as Walmart and Best Buy frequently run competing promotions around the time of Prime Day, so it’s worth comparing prices before buying.
Prime Day is available in multiple countries, including Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, China, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Luxembourg, Mexico, the Netherlands, Portugal, Singapore, Spain, the U.K., and the U.S.


						

							


Why you can trust Macworld’s recommendations
The Prime Day iPad deals picked here are all chosen by our editors, who have decades of experience with Apple devices. We’ve reviewed everything we recommend, and we won’t tell you to buy something that’s not an actual deal. We track current prices against previous lows and only highlight discounts we think are worth considering. During Prime Day, we continually update this page as better deals appear, selecting the configurations that offer the best value for each product type. Apple products are expensive, so we focus on prices we’d be willing to pay ourselves—and deals we believe will genuinely save you money.


						

							




Prime Day 2026: More outstanding Apple deals
Throughout the Prime Day sale, we constantly check Amazon’s listings to find the best deals. We’ve tested all of the models we recommend here and only select the very best deals—so if you see an iPad listed here, you’ll know it’s at or near its all-time low price. And it’s not just iPads.

title: Mac Users Reclaim 12GB+ of Storage With Apple Intelligence Removal Tool
content:
A new open-source tool is making waves in the Mac community by helping users reclaim valuable storage space taken up by Apple's AI models. Called "RemoveMacAI," the command line tool disables Apple Intelligence on macOS 27, removes its downloaded models, and prevents them from being downloaded again.


In macOS 27, Apple removed the toggle to disable Apple Intelligence wholesale, and simply disabling individual features doesn't remove the models from your Mac's drive. As explained by the developer, RemoveMacAI gets around this by using a configuration profile to switch off Apple's own asset management service and remove the models. 

It then configures the system so attempts to download the removed models are redirected to a closed local port, preventing them from immediately coming back. And it does all this without disabling System Integrity Protection (SIP) or manually deleting files from protected system locations, unlike some older tools have.

The tool can free up roughly 12GB of space depending on which models are present on your Mac. That said, some users are reporting cases of Apple Intelligence models having taken up a lot more space, which they've now reclaimed. 

With the Apple models gone, you lose all Siri-related AI features, Writing Tools, Genmoji, Image Playground, ChatGPT integration, summaries, smart replies, inline predictions, Photos Clean Up, Spatial Photos, and Xcode predictive completion. Even so, plenty of users appear happy to make the sacrifice to free up space, especially on non-upgradeable Macs with 256GB of storage. The profile reportedly persists across updates. And if you're wondering, dictation still works. There's also a revert command to restore everything AI-related.

GitHub stars since its release last week, and there's lots of discussion on Reddit and Hacker News about the need for such a tool. Just be aware that MacRumors isn't endorsing RemoveMacAI, and anyone using it does so at their own risk.

title: Apple’s next big thing may be even riskier than the iPhone Duo
content:
Macworld





This time next week, the Apple world could look very different. We may have received (and doubtless be obsessing over the artwork and tagline of) invitations to an event on October 13, when reputable sources say the company will unveil its next big thing. Or, based on other clues, namely the arrival in Apple retail stores of mysterious boxes to be opened on October 8, the information may have already emerged.
Whether it appears this Thursday or next Tuesday, and whether it’s announced via a big press event or a humble press release, Apple’s next big thing will almost certainly be its first bona fide smart-home product: a hub, made up of a vaguely HomePod-like speaker topped by a vaguely iPad-like screen. We in the media have taken to calling it the HomePad, but if the recent launches of the MacBook Neo and iPhone Duo are anything to go by, Apple will probably call it something short and cute and random, ending with an O. The HomePod Echo, perhaps. Or perhaps not.
The real issue with the HomePad is not its name, but its niche. Potential customers will ask every marketing manager’s most feared question: What is it for? If Apple hasn’t come up with an answer in the multiple years the product has been in development, it’s unlikely something will spring to mind in the next eight days. But one way or another an answer will be needed.
As I hinted with my silly Echo joke, this isn’t an unprecedented concept or a new market. Amazon’s closest rival is probably the Echo Show 8 (the Show 5 is closer in screen size, but has a different design), while Google has the Nest Hub, and both sit in the space Apple will be looking to dominate. The presence of these incumbents might seem like a good omen for the company, which loves to wait until a market is established before taking a swing with the definitive product. But as with the foldable iPhone Duo, there are two problems: First, while tech fans in general are intimately familiar with the concept, Apple’s own fans are not. And second, Apple’s version is likely to be more expensive.
The original HomePod may be an illustrative comparison here. Apple was expected to go after the smart speaker market, but ended up leaning far more on the second word than the first. The HomePod is sort of smart, but it’s really just a nice, decent-quality speaker you can command (some of the time…) using your voice. And so Apple didn’t end up displacing products like the Echo and the Nest because the HomePod couldn’t do what they do and didn’t really try, while overachieving in other areas and costing more. And Apple customers, unless they were bold enough to become platform-agnostic, remained outside that bubble.
Siri is a lot smarter now than it was then (not that you’d know it from the performance of legacy HomePod models, unfortunately), so the chances are that Apple will try to do the smart-home concept properly this time. The HomePad will run Siri AI, and thus be able to field questions, surface information from your messages and email inbox, and use natural language. It will have excellent capabilities. But again, the question is what we will use these capabilities for. Where will it sit? What functions will it perform? Speaking personally, I’m not sure how it would fit in my life. So the product’s introduction will need to do a great deal of imaginative heavy lifting.
Let’s say the HomePad sits in the kitchen. Useful for recipes, perhaps, although it’s important to remember that it will only have a 6-inch screen and thus won’t match an iPad for legibility. Or it might sit in the living room and act as the hub for smart-home controls. But what proportion of Apple fans actually use HomeKit smart lights, smart door locks, and a smart thermostat so much that they need a dedicated device? A relatively small one, I’d guess, and those that do will be accustomed to controlling them via automations or manual control on an iPhone. Or even voice controls via a HomePod.
At least with the iPhone Duo, Apple had some user experience to lean on. It is, after all, still a phone, albeit one that’s a little smaller than we’re used to, with the ability to offer a bigger screen than we’re used to. But customers get what it’s offering. It’s a phone, only conceptually better. (And pragmatically, in some ways, rather worse.) You don’t need to make such an imaginative leap of faith.
But the HomePad doesn’t really have a precedent in Apple’s walled garden. It’s a HomePod with a screen. But having a screen (and offering voice control which actually works) massively expands its capabilities in one area, while cutting the speaker down to a tiny hemisphere, as is predicted, slashes them in another. What we end up with isn’t remotely like a HomePod in form or function. It’s something new. And new is scary.
So Apple’s crack marketing team has another challenge on their hands. If you thought the iPhone Duo was an exciting, radical, risky product, wait for the HomePad.
Or whatever they end up calling it. Something short and cute and random. Ending with an O.

title: iPhone 18 Pro & Max Guide: Everything you need to know about the new iPhones
content:
Macworld





The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max are now on sale. They retain the 6.3-inch and 6.9-inch screen sizes and aluminum unibody design introduced with the previous generation, but Apple has made substantial changes to the cameras, processor, cooling, battery life and connectivity.
The biggest camera upgrade is a new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture, which can automatically move between ƒ/1.48, ƒ/1.8, ƒ/2.8 and ƒ/4 depending on lighting and depth of field. The widest aperture lets in more light for low-light photography, while new Pro controls let users manually adjust aperture, shutter speed and white balance, and view a histogram to assess exposure.
Inside is the A20 Pro, Apple’s first iPhone chip made using a 2nm process. It has a new six-core CPU, seven-core GPU, Dual 16-core Neural Engine and 50% more memory bandwidth than the A19 Pro. A larger vapor chamber and new M-series-inspired chip packaging also improve heat dissipation, with Apple claiming up to 40% better sustained performance than the iPhone 17 Pro.
Other major changes include up to 36 hours of Apple-rated video playback on the Pro and 45 hours on the Pro Max on eSIM-only models, faster wired charging, and a redesigned Dynamic Island capable of showing three Live Activities simultaneously. The iPhone 18 Pro uses Apple’s new C2 cellular modem worldwide. The Pro Max also uses C2 outside the U.S., but teardown analysis has confirmed that the U.S. iPhone 18 Pro Max retains Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X80 modem – more on that below.
Since launch, some owners have also reported problems including unexpected restarts, touchscreen freezes and speaker crackling or popping. Apple addressed several early issues in iOS 27.0.1, although the cause of the reported speaker problem remains unclear.
iPhone 18 Pro/Max vs iPhone 17 Pro/Max: Top 10 changes at a glance

				
					

				
			iPhone 18 Pro vs iPhone 17 Pro
Foundry




The five biggest changes are the variable-aperture camera, A20 Pro, improved cooling, longer battery life and redesigned Dynamic Island/connectivity system. Here is an overview of what’s new compared to the previous generation.

Apple has added a 2TB option to the smaller Pro for the first time, while retaining 256GB as the entry-level capacity.


When is the iPhone 18 Pro coming out? Availability and how to buy
The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max were announced on Wednesday, September 9, 2026 and started shipping on Friday, September 18, 2026 in more than 65 countries and regions and in another 20 countries from Friday September 25.
You can buy the phones directly from Apple online or at Apple Stores, as well as through mobile networks and authorized Apple retailers. Apple sells unlocked iPhones directly through its website and stores. We have tips on when is the Best time to buy an iPhone if you want to get the best deal or avoid buying just before a new iPhone launches.

Buy iPhone 18 Pro and Max at Apple U.K. 
							

										
									Read our review

$1299 at  Apple						
					


						

							


iPhone 18 Pro problems: What owners are reporting
Owners of the new iPhone 18 Pro models have already reported a number of issues since the phones went on sale.
It isn’t clear how widespread these problems are, but Apple released iOS 27.0.1 on September 28 with fixes for several issues affecting the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.
If you’re experiencing any of the problems addressed by the update, install iOS 27.0.1 via Settings > General > Software Update. 
Cellular problems on some AT&T iPhone 18 Pro Max phones
Apple has confirmed that a small number of iPhone 18 Pro Max devices on AT&T can lose cellular service, preventing calls, texts and data access, potentially including 911 calls. Complaints began shortly after launch, with some users reporting their phones dropping into SOS mode despite showing a strong 5G signal. 
Apple says owners should install iOS 27.0.1 as well as a new carrier settings update. Together, the updates are intended to prevent the problem from occurring. The carrier update should install automatically within 14 days, or users can check manually by going to Settings > General > About. 
However, the updates cannot repair phones that have already lost service because of the issue. Apple says affected devices cannot be reactivated through software and will need to be replaced, with customers advised to contact Apple or AT&T for assistance.
The exact cause remains unknown. One key difference is that the U.S. iPhone 18 Pro Max uses Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X80 modem, while the iPhone 18 Pro uses Apple’s C2 modem, but there is no evidence that Qualcomm hardware itself is to blame. The X80 was also used without this problem in earlier iPhones, and the issue appears more likely to involve the way the phone’s software and hardware interact with AT&T’s network.
Unexpected restarts after Face ID failed to authenticate
Some ownersApple says iOS 27.0.1 addresses the touchscreen problem reported that their phones would freeze and restart after a failed Face ID attempt, particularly when trying to unlock protected apps.
According to Apple’s release notes for iOS 27.0.1, the update fixes an issue that could cause an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max to unexpectedly restart after Face ID failed to authenticate.
Camera color artifact bug
iOS 27.0.1 also fixes a camera bug that could cause a color artifact to appear in photos taken at 2x under certain lighting conditions at f/1.48 on a small number of iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max devices.
Touchscreen problem
Some owners reported a problem with the iPhone 18 Pro’s screen where opening Notification Center and Control Center simultaneously could cause the display to become unresponsive.
Apple says iOS 27.0.1 fixes the touchscreen problem.
Speaker crackling and popping
Some iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max owners are reporting intermittent crackling, popping, or clicking sounds from the phone’s speakers, particularly the earpiece during calls. Reports on Apple’s support forums describe the problem occurring randomly rather than on every call, with some users saying that restarting the iPhone temporarily clears it. Others have encountered similar noises during video calls or while using certain apps.
It isn’t yet clear whether the problem is caused by the iPhone 18 Pro hardware or by iOS 27. There are reports of replacement phones exhibiting the same behavior, while at least one user has reported similar call-quality problems on an older iPhone after updating to iOS 27, raising the possibility that software is involved.
iOS 27.0.1 does not appear to address the issue, and Apple has not publicly confirmed a cause or fix at this stage.


						

							


iPhone 18 Pro/Max design: What does it look like?

				
					

				
			
This is the Burgundy variant (we think Deep Cherry was a much nicer name).

Foundry




The iPhone 18 Pro retains the aluminum unibody introduced with the iPhone 17 Pro, as well as the Ceramic Shield on the rear and Ceramic Shield 2 over the display. The camera system remains arranged on the large raised plateau across the upper part of the rear casing.
Screen sizes are unchanged at 6.3 inches for the iPhone 18 Pro and 6.9 inches for the iPhone 18 Pro Max, both using Super Retina XDR OLED displays with ProMotion up to 120Hz.
Apple offers four finishes this year:
Burgundy 
Glacier
Silver
Black
That means Cosmic Orange and Deep Blue disappear, while black returns to the Pro line despite pre-launch reports suggesting it would not. Read more about the color choices here: Apple’s new iPhone 18 Pro colors.
The pre-event leaks suggested the basic chassis dimensions would remain very close to the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max, with the camera plateau rather than the body itself becoming thicker. We can confirm from our own research that the newer camera bump is approximately 0.5mm taller. This means that cases designed for the iPhone 17 Pro may not fit the iPhone 18 Pro. Before buying a case, check compatibility and  read our Best iPhone 18 Pro cases buying guide.
The new iPhones share the same screen sizes and overall form as their predecessors, but both models are slightly heavier this time. 
iPhone 18 Pro dimensions: 150 x 71.9 x 8.75mm / 5.91 x 2.83 x 0.34 in
iPhone 18 Pro weight: 7.44 ounces / 211 grams (17 Pro was 7.27 ounces / 206 grams with eSIM)
iPhone 18 Pro Max dimensions: 163.4 x 78 x 8.75mm / 6.43 x 3.07 x 0.34 in
iPhone 18 Pro Max weight: 8.78 ounces / 249 grams (17 Pro Max was 8.22 ounces / 233 grams with eSIM)
Changes to the Dynamic Island
Apple has redesigned the Dynamic Island. Apple says new display technology creates additional usable space and allows the Dynamic Island to display up to three Live Activities at once, for example navigation, music and a sports score.
Apple has not announced fully under-display Face ID. Pre-launch reports suggested that one or more infrared Face ID components could move beneath the OLED panel, allowing the notch to shrink, but Apple hasn’t confirmed the underlying sensor arrangement.


						

							


iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max cameras: Are the cameras the same?

				
					

				
			
The iPhone 18 Pro cameras.

Apple




Both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max have the same three-camera rear system. The main change is not resolution—all three remain 48MP—but the new variable-aperture Main camera and new computational imaging pipeline.
The three most notable camera upgrades are:
Variable aperture on the 48MP Main camera.
A new Main camera sensor and imaging pipeline, improving low-light performance and detail.
More extensive manual Pro controls, including aperture, shutter speed, white balance and histogram.


						

							




Rear cameras


CameraResolutionFocal lengthAperturePixel information
Fusion Main48MP sensor; 12MP at 2x optical-quality zoom24mm / 48mm, 1x / 2xƒ/1.48, ƒ/1.8, ƒ/2.8, ƒ/4 variable2.44μm quad-pixel / 1.22μm individual
Fusion Ultra Wide48MP13mm, 0.5x / macroƒ/2.21.4μm quad-pixel / 0.7μm individual
Fusion Telephoto48MP sensor; 12MP at 8x optical-quality zoom100mm / 200mm, 4x / 8xƒ/2.81.4μm quad-pixel / 0.7μm individual

 



The 2x and 8x optical-quality options use crops from the Main and Telephoto sensors respectively, producing 12MP images rather than 48MP captures.
The Main camera’s six-blade mechanical aperture can automatically open to ƒ/1.48 in low light or close as far as ƒ/4 for increased depth of field. Photographers can also select aperture manually.
An iFixIt teardown revealed that the mechanical aperture uses six overlapping, extremely thin blades controlled inside the camera assembly. The mechanism itself is unlikely to be repairable individually if it fails, meaning the complete camera module will probably need to be replaced.
Both Pro models also offer up to 8x optical-quality zoom from the Telephoto camera. Contrary to some earlier rumors, the variable-aperture camera is not exclusive to the Pro Max.


Photography and editing improvements
Computational photography: Apple has introduced a new imaging pipeline, smart focus tracking, improved Clean Up, Spatial Reframing, an Extend tool and Photographic Styles 3, which adds texture and grain adjustments. These controls require photos captured on iPhone 18 Pro/Max or the Duo’s Main, Ultra Wide or Center Stage cameras. Older supported iPhones can edit those eligible images—it isn’t simply a restriction on the editing device. See: Apple’s next-gen photo controls only work on images ‘captured’ on a new iPhone.
Apple Reference Image (U.S. and U.K.): Will use signed data from the iPhone 18 Pro’s Main camera sensor to create an unalterable reference image through Private Cloud Compute. Viewed alongside the edited photo in Photos, it helps users assess what has changed, providing a useful authenticity check for photographers, journalists and anyone sharing images. It’s off by default, to enable it go to: Settings > Camera > Reference Image > Add Reference Mode.
Front camera
Apple has retained the 18MP Center Stage front camera, rather than moving to the rumored 24MP sensor. It supports automatic reframing, Center Stage, ultra-stabilized video and Dual Capture.
The front camera remains visibly associated with the Dynamic Island. Apple has not announced an under-display selfie camera on the iPhone 18 Pro.
iPhone 18 Pro video changes
Frame rates: Cinematic effects can now be applied after shooting to ordinary videos captured at up to 60fps. The phones continue to offer 4K 120fps Dolby Vision for high-frame-rate shooting.
Time-lapse: Time-lapse receives a significant upgrade to 4K with Dolby Vision HDR.


						

							


A20 Pro processor: How fast is it?

				
					

				
			
Apple has redesigned the iPhone chip. 

Apple




Both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max use Apple’s new A20 Pro processor.
It is manufactured using a 2-nanometer process, down from the 3nm-class process used for A19 Pro, giving Apple more scope to improve efficiency and transistor density.
The chip includes:
6-core CPU
7-core GPU
Neural Accelerators integrated into the CPU/GPU architecture
Dual 16-core Neural Engine, 32 cores in total
50% more memory bandwidth than A19 Pro
Apple says the GPU is up to 40% faster than A19 Pro, while the Neural Engine offers roughly double the AI processing capability.
One particularly important change is the packaging. Inspired by Apple’s M-series Mac chips, A20 Pro places the processor die side-by-side with memory rather than stacking memory directly in the chip’s thermal path. This improves heat transfer and allows the processor to couple more directly to the vapor chamber.
That vapor chamber itself has three times the surface area of the iPhone 17 Pro’s system. Apple claims the combination delivers up to 40% better sustained performance, which should be most noticeable during gaming, video work and intensive on-device AI rather than ordinary web browsing and messaging.
During our review, the iPhone 18 Pro showed noticeably less heat buildup than the iPhone 17 Pro when playing demanding games, recording extended video and performing other prolonged intensive tasks. It still became warm. This was our reviewer’s observation during use, rather than a measured temperature reduction or a quantified test of Apple’s sustained-performance claim.


						

							


RAM: How much memory does the iPhone 18 Pro/Max have?
Apple does not officially publish RAM capacities for iPhones. However, iFixIt lists 12GB of LPDDR5X memory for both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, matching the reported 12GB in the previous Pro generation.
The main memory upgrade is bandwidth: Apple says the A20 Pro offers 50% more memory bandwidth than A19 Pro. This increases the amount of data its CPU, GPU and Neural Engine can transfer to and from memory each second.
Higher memory bandwidth can help accelerate demanding tasks, including on-device AI. Combined with the redesigned chip packaging and improved cooling, it should help sustain performance during intensive workloads. However, this does not necessarily mean that more Apple Intelligence or Siri AI tasks run locally rather than in the cloud.


						

							


iPhone 18 Pro/Max connectivity options 
C2 modem
The iPhone 18 Pro introduces Apple’s C2 cellular modem, replacing the Qualcomm modem used in the previous Pro generation. 
Apple says C2 delivers faster uploads while consuming 15% less energy than C1X, alongside AI-powered improvements to connection quality and reliability and support for mmWave in the U.S.
The exception is the U.S. iPhone 18 Pro Max. iFixIt’s teardowns have confirmed that this version retains Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X80 modem, while Pro Max models sold elsewhere use Apple’s C2. Apple has not explained the regional difference.
Wi-Fi and Bluetooth
Like the predecessors, the 2026 iPhones use Apple’s N1 wireless networking chip, supporting:
Wi-Fi 7
Bluetooth 6
Thread
Satellite
Emergency SOS via satellite, Messages via satellite, Roadside Assistance via satellite and Find My satellite functionality continue. Apple made no announcements about full satellite internet or ordinary 5G data delivered by satellite, despite pre-launch rumors suggesting such a capability could appear.


						

							


iPhone 18 Pro/Max Battery, MagSafe and charging: What’s changed?
Battery life is one of the most significant improvements.
Apple says eSIM-only models gain additional battery capacity because the space previously occupied by the physical SIM tray can be used for battery cells. Physical-SIM variants provide around two hours less video playback than equivalent eSIM-only models.
Battery-life improvements come from larger batteries and greater power efficiency, including the new 2nm A20 Pro processor.


						

							




iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max battery capacity and life
The table below compares battery capacity and Apple’s video-playback ratings for the physical-SIM and eSIM-only versions of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.


ModelSIM versionBattery capacityEnergyVideo playbackEquivalent iPhone 17 model: video playbackImprovement

iPhone 18 ProPhysical SIM4,056mAh15.86WhUp to 34 hours17 Pro: up to 31 hours+3 hours
iPhone 18 ProeSIM-only4,288mAh16.76WhUp to 36 hours17 Pro: up to 33 hours+3 hours
iPhone 18 Pro MaxPhysical SIM5,391mAh21.06WhUp to 43 hours17 Pro Max: up to 37 hours+6 hours
iPhone 18 Pro MaxeSIM-only5,567mAh21.75WhUp to 45 hours17 Pro Max: up to 39 hours+6 hours

 



We discuss the battery life for different iPhones in more depth separately. 


Wired charging
Wired charging is faster. Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max can reach 50% charge in around 15 minutes when using a USB-C cable and a 60W-capable or higher power adapter that supports Adjustable Voltage Supply (AVS). The adapter is sold separately. This compares with around 20 minutes for the iPhone 17 Pro generation. Apple also says five minutes of wired charging can provide around seven hours of video playback on the iPhone 18 Pro Max.
Our charging tests also showed an improvement: the iPhone 18 Pro reached 80 percent charge about 10 minutes sooner than the iPhone 17 Pro, and a full charge almost 20 minutes sooner. These results apply to the smaller Pro model.
MagSafe and wireless charging
Apple says both models can reach 50% charge in around 30 minutes using a MagSafe Charger paired with a 35W or higher power adapter, both sold separately. MagSafe and Qi2 wireless charging support up to 25W. Wireless charging speeds are broadly unchanged from the iPhone 17 Pro generation.


						

							


iPhone 18 Pro software: iOS 27 and Siri AI 
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max support Siri AI in iOS 27, but the upgraded assistant isn’t enabled automatically. 
To request access, open Settings > Siri, enable Siri if necessary, then tap Try Siri AI (Beta). 
Then follow the setup instructions to join Apple’s waiting list. 
Access may arrive within minutes, hours or days, with a notification when it’s ready. 
Your device and Siri languages must both be English, and availability depends on your Apple Account region. You may also need up to 14GB of free storage. See how to get Siri AI for setup instructions and details of regional restrictions.


						

							




iPhone 18 Pro price: How much does it cost?
Apple has increased prices by $100 in the U.S. and £100 in the U.K. 
The iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199/£1,199, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299/£1,299. Both begin with 256GB of storage.

iPhone Pro$1,199/£1,199$1,099/£1,099+$100/£100
iPhone Pro Max$1,299/£1,299$1,199/£1,199+$100/£100

 



Apple offers both models with 256GB, 512GB, 1TB and 2TB. That means the entry-level storage remains 256GB rather than increasing again. The notable change is that 2TB is now available on both models; previously the iPhone 17 Pro topped out at 1TB while the Pro Max could be configured with 2TB.
The $100 increase is considerably smaller than some analyst predictions before launch. Those forecasts had pointed to sharply higher DRAM and NAND costs caused by the global memory shortage, with estimates that the cost of 12GB of DRAM alone could rise dramatically this year. That makes component and memory pricing a credible contributor to Apple’s increase, although Apple itself hasn’t attributed the higher price to any one component.


Should you buy the iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max? Which model should you choose?

				
					

				
			
Which one do you want?

Apple




The iPhone 18 Pro is the better-value Pro model for most buyers, offering the same cameras and A20 Pro processor as the Pro Max in a more manageable 6.3-inch design. Choose the Pro Max if its 6.9-inch display and longer battery life justify the extra $100/£100 and additional weight. Apple rates it for up to 45 hours of video playback on eSIM-only models, or 43 hours on physical-SIM versions.
However, you may not need a Pro iPhone at all. Our best iPhone guide recommends the standard iPhone 17 for most people: its ProMotion display, dual 48MP cameras and 256GB of storage cover everyday needs for considerably less. Paying extra for the 18 Pro makes most sense if you want its dedicated Telephoto camera, variable aperture or additional performance for demanding games and creative work.
iPhone 17 Pro owners don’t need to rush to upgrade. Consider whether the variable-aperture Main camera, A20 Pro, improved cooling, faster charging and longer battery life will make enough difference to justify the expense. If your current phone comfortably handles everything you do, keeping it is a sensible choice.
For iPhone 14 Pro owners and earlier, the accumulated improvements make a stronger case. You gain USB-C, Apple Intelligence compatibility, higher-resolution Ultra Wide and Telephoto cameras, an improved front camera, larger displays and slimmer bezels. These changes span several generations: USB-C and the Action button arrived before Camera Control and the larger Pro displays, while the 18MP Center Stage front camera was already available on the iPhone 17 Pro. Apple Intelligence also supports the iPhone 15 Pro and later compatible models. This year’s variable aperture, A20 Pro and further battery improvements build on those earlier upgrades. Read why the iPhone 18 Pro rewards those who waited.
The iPhone Duo is worth considering if screen space and multitasking matter more than camera versatility. Its folding display and Split View offer something the Pro models cannot, but its $1,999/£1,999 starting price is $800/£800 above the smaller Pro. Despite that premium, it lacks a dedicated Telephoto camera and variable aperture. Choose the Duo for its folding design; choose a Pro for photography and better value. Our iPhone buying guide compares the specifications.
Both Pro models are now on sale, making this a good point in their release cycle to buy. If saving money matters more than upgrading immediately, Black Friday may bring better trade-in or carrier offers, although large outright discounts are unlikely so soon after launch. A substantially discounted iPhone 17 Pro is another option. See the best time to buy an iPhone.


						

							


Did Apple launch the iPhone 18?
There was no new iPhone 18 at the event. We expect the iPhone 18 to launch alongside the iPhone 18e and iPhone Air 2 in spring 2027. Read more about the iPhone 18 here: iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e: Release date, rumored specs and more.

title: Apple's New CEO John Ternus is Making Product Design a 'Major Priority'
content:
Since becoming Apple's CEO last month, John Ternus has made product design a "major priority," according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. 


"Ternus already had some involvement with the design studio as Apple's head of hardware engineering, given the close coordination required between the two functions," he said, in his Power On newsletter today. "Since becoming CEO, however, he has immersed himself in the industrial design and human interface teams."

Ternus goes "hands-on" in Apple's design studio "several times a week, sometimes visiting multiple times in a single day," whereas Apple's former CEO Tim Cook typically visited the studio for "about an hour once a month, at most," according to Gurman.

Unlike Cook, who is better known as a supply chain expert, Ternus comes from an engineering background. As such, Gurman said that Ternus is largely leaving Apple's finances to financial chief Kevan Parekh and its supply chain to operations chief Sabih Khan, giving him more time to focus on engineering and design.
